Dicevaders lets you destroy earth with dice, out now on iOS

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, dicevaders sees you taking on the role not of defender of the Earth, but of its invaders and destroyers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as we head towards the weekend, it's becoming increasingly cold and dark, and that means you'll probably want to sit and find a mobile game to sink plenty of time into. Well, you're in luck, because there's a constant glut of great newly introduced releases, including the launch of Dicevaders on iOS!

In a recent development, dicevaders sees you taking on the role not of defender of the Earth, but of its invaders and destroyers. To do so, you'll need to gradually overwhelm the defences of each of Earth's bastions, and you'll do so with dice (naturally). In essence, you place units, build up multipliers and gradually overcome the defence rating of each planet to destroy it.

Recent findings suggest that it makes for a rather interesting combination of luck and strategy, where you'll need to think about when you might need to reroll and keep your supply of currencies stocked up to do so. The graphics are, of course, the kind of crunchy, colourful pixels I'm fond of, so you won't hear any complaints from me, and the mix of blues, purples and reds makes for a thoroughly alien colour palette.

There's plenty of synergy, different commanders and units to take advantage of too. So if you're looking for a game with plenty of depth to enjoy this winter, why not check out Dicevaders on iOS?

Looking to put your strategic acumen to the test? Want to rely on raw numbers rather than the randomness of dice? Then be sure to check out our list of the best strategy games on iOS!

Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major enhancement.
  • Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys.
  • Industry observers note that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major enhancement. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

Industry observers note that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the massive focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

In a recent development, the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

In a recent development, ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a fresh activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

10 Great Games That Defined The Nintendo Wii

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1505 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 20 years ago, Nintendo launched one of their most ambitious consoles of all time with the motion control-focused and internet connected Nintendo Wii.
  • Sources indicate that designed to be the most accessible console ever made for its era, the Wii became one of Nintendo’s greatest success stories.
  • However, Nintendo’s resurgence and the Wii’s global popularity wouldn’t have occurred had it not been for the wide variety of exclusive games that launched on the console and went on to define the Wii as well as Nintendo’s future prospects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

20 years ago, Nintendo launched one of their most ambitious consoles of all time with the motion control-focused and internet connected Nintendo Wii.

Sources indicate that designed to be the most accessible console ever made for its era, the Wii became one of Nintendo’s greatest success stories. Its easy to understand controls created a phenomenon of people of all ages getting into console gaming for the first time, from children to senior citizens.

However, Nintendo’s resurgence and the Wii’s global popularity wouldn’t have occurred had it not been for the wide variety of exclusive games that launched on the console and went on to define the Wii as well as Nintendo’s future prospects.

When people think of gaming rivalries, most people will think of the console wars between Nintendo and Sega in the 1980s and 1990s. While that conflict ended with the failure of the Sega Dreamcast, the two gaming brands’ mascots wouldn’t officially meet until 2007’s Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games.

Made to coincide with the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games was the first official crossover between the Super Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog franchises, with characters from both properties being able to compete in archery, fencing, rowing, and other Olympic events.

Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games not only represents the growing comradery between Nintendo and other video game publishers but also how much pure, simplistic fun can be had on the Wii by being able to play as some of gaming’s greatest icons in jovial sports competitions.

Industry observers note that one of the best series of games to debut with the Wii was Shigeru Miyamoto's “Wii Project” which was a series of typically Mii-centric games tailored to showcase the Wii’s controls and accessibility to more casual gamers. One of the best of these games being Wii Play.

A Wii launch title for European and Asian markets, Wii Play was essentially a Mario Party-like compilation of minigames designed to highlight the versatility of the Wiimote in games such as the Duck Hunt-like Shooting Range, Billiards, Fishing, Find Mii, and more.

On a more personal note, my favorite of these minigames was the top-down Atari Combat-like Tanks! which has one or two players control tanks through toy block stages to destroy enemy tanks using the Wiimote’s D-pad.

In 2006, Nintendo revolutionized mobile 2D side-scrolling Super Mario games with the release of Latest Super Mario Bros. for the Nintendo DS. To capitalize on that game’s success, Nintendo decided to create a multiplayer, console-based sequel, in the form of 2009’s New Super Mario Bros. Wii.

It has been revealed that the first new console-based 2D Mario game since 1995’s Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island, New Super Mario Bros. Wii was a near perfect translation of New Super Mario Bros. enhanced platforming gameplay to the Wii, with the added bonus of four-player local co-op featuring Mario, Luigi, Blue Toad, and Yellow Toad.

It has been revealed that in fact, New Super Mario Bros. Wii might have been too perfect of a game, as Nintendo essentially kept on remastering it for years on end until the release of Super Mario Bros. Wonder. The former game was essentially ported to the Wii U and Nintendo Switch in the form of New Super Mario Bros. U, New Super Luigi U, and New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe.

Many latest exclusive games made their debut on the Wii, but arguably the most creative and cinematic of them was Monolith Soft’s third-person action role-playing game Xenoblade Chronicles.

According to recent reports, A spinoff of the long-running Xeno series, Xenoblade Chronicles is set in a sci-fi fantasy world where life eventually evolved on two titanic robots, the Bionis and the Mechonis, that have laid dormant for millennia. The situation led to lifeforms from both robots fighting each other in perpetual wars.

While Xenoblade Chronicles may not have been the best looking RPG on the market in 2010, it more than made up for its blurry visuals with its enthralling narrative, centered around the orphaned hero Shulk and his mysterious Monado sword, as well as its more open-world structured gameplay.

In a recent development, ever since Nintendo released the hit fighting game Super Smash Bros. Melee on the GameCube, expectations were high for its sequel. While many players would consider Super Smash Bros. Brawl to be a disappointing sequel, it still managed to delight series newcomers in many ways.

It has been revealed that like previous Super Smash Bros. titles, Super Smash Bros. Brawl is a crossover fighting game pitting Nintendo’s most famous characters against each other. Brawl innovated upon the series in many ways, such as featuring non-Nintendo characters like Sonic and Snake as well as featuring a stage builder.

Sources indicate that however, what really made Brawl an epic game in the eyes of many Wii fans was its cinematic campaign, The Subspace Emissary. It depicts many of gaming's most celebrated icons fighting and joining forces together to defeat the united destructive forces of Bowser, Ganondorf, Master Hand, and Tabuu.

Sources indicate that it's rare for video game series to never have a bad entry, especially one as long as Mario Kart, but the hit racing series has consistently managed to release banger after banger. In 2008, the Mario Kart game everybody needed to have was Mario Kart Wii.

The follow-up to the hit Mario Kart DS, Mario Kart Wii was innovative for the series in many ways, as it featured 24 player characters including customized Miis, motorcycles, and was the first home console MK game to feature online multiplayer.

Sources indicate that what made Mario Kart Wii especially fun and the second best-selling Wii game was its Wii Wheel accessory. While it didn’t alter gameplay in any way, the Wii Wheel helped immerse players into the feeling of actually racing with friends online and in-person.

Industry observers note that in the same vein as Wii Play, Shigeru Miyamoto strove to expand upon his “Wii Project” in 2007 by creating a game that would encourage families to exercise. He more or less succeeded with Wii Fit.

Primarily played through the packed-in Wii Balance Board, Wii Fit is a fairly relaxing exercise video game centered around players practicing yoga poses, strength training, aerobics, and balance on the Board, with the game further tracking people’s weight and fitness progress.

Wii Fit certainly didn’t make anyone exceptionally strong, but it did motivate millions of people to become more invested in their overall health, and it did lead many friends and family to start exercising together consistently.

Recent findings suggest that while Wii Fit didn’t make most players work up a sweat, Ubisoft Paris’ music rhythm game Just Dance certainly did, and laid the groundwork for the Wii’s longest running support. Just Dance titles would release for the console well into the eighth and ninth console generations.

Initially a Wii exclusive series, Just Dance was an expansion upon dance pad games like Dance Dance Revolution, instead having players mirror the moves of on-screen dancers as best as possible with the Wiimote tracking players' motions.

While Just Dance 1 only had a modest tracklist of 33 songs that could be played across four similar modes, it laid the groundwork for a dancing video game phenomenon that’s still going strong today; one of Ubisoft and Nintendo’s most popular series among casual and hardcore gamers alike.

Industry observers note that at Space World 2000, Nintendo publicly revealed the Super Mario 128 project as a GameCube tech demo, featuring 128 Marios running around a spherical surface. While much of this project would be utilized in Pikmin, it wasn’t fully realized until the release of 2007’s Super Mario Galaxy.

The third 3D Super Mario game, Super Mario Galaxy was one of the most ambitious entries in the franchise, as not only did it feature a more cinematic storyline centered around Rosalina and the star-like Lumas, but had players travel across the galaxy on spherical planetoids.

Industry observers note that this game design may have been nauseating for some players, but Super Mario Galaxy continued to show how the 3D Mario titles always strive to innovate upon each other to deliver creative, generation-defining experiences. The game even went on to directly inspire The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.

Without a doubt, the game that best defined the fun to be had on the Wii was arguably the greatest launch title of all time, Wii Sports.

The first entry in Shigeru Miyamoto's “Wii Project”, Wii Sports was a rather simplistic collection of sports games centered around customizable Miis playing tennis, baseball, bowling, golf, and boxing, in single-player or up to four-player local co-op.

However, Wii Sports’ simplistic design worked to its favor, as it allowed gamers of all ages and walks of life to easily play the game. The likes of Wii Sports bowling and tennis still being played by thousands of gamers worldwide 20 years later, in their original forms and within new titles in the series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Upgrade 18/11: Crystal Dynamics have provided the following statement to RPS, confirming it cut eight staff members:.

The original article continues below.

Sources indicate that as initially reported by Vertical Slice (thanks, Chris!), the workforce of Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is being cut as part of a new set of layoffs by owners Embracer. As far as is right now known, those affected include senior game designer Joshua Mitchell, senior environment technical artist Kevin Baker, and UI software engineer Garin R. K. Richards, all of whom shared news of their redunancies on LinkedIn. There may be more affected, but neither Crystal Dynamics nor Embracer have offered comments on the reduction of staff as yet.

Industry observers note that this now marks the studio's fifth round of layoffs since Embracer acquired it in 2022, following cuts in March 2025, August 2025, November 2025, and March this year. This is a drastic amount even considering the current state of the industry, with layoffs seemingly happening several times a week, but unfortunately, this is par for the course for Embracer. Even still, it makes one wonder just how many staff are left at Crystal Dynamics by now. Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and Tomb Raider: Catalyst are still in production, so you'd hope that the studio won't be shuttered entirely.

Sources indicate that according to Legacy of Atlantis' Steam page, generative AI has been used in the development of Legacy of Atlantis "to support some early exploration and temporary development content. Any AI-assisted assets were either replaced or refined by humans in order to maintain the creative and artistic vision of the development team." I would hope that this isn't a case of Embracer cutting staff in the misguided hope that they can just be replaced with the use of genAI, but who can say. Solidarity to those affected, who I hope can find latest work soon.

Industry observers note that while cosy may be a term bordering on the pejorative nowadays, that doesn't mean there aren't plenty of cracking games out there to play in the genre. A case in point is Tiny Bookshop, a great game for any fan of literature and a good bookstore. Now, developer Neoludic Games is celebrating one million copies sold, with an all-new DLC coming soon!

Industry observers note that arts & Crafts, the newly introduced DLC for Tiny Bookshop, is set to arrive later this month. Don't expect any massive new changes, like a roguelike dungeon-crawling mode. But you will find two new locations to visit, with the introduction of Puffin Primary and the Artist Quarter, not to mention 24 new wagon parts and 30 decoration items.

While it may not be my cup of tea, it's not hard to see why Tiny Bookshop has sold over a million copies, and doubtless its widespread release on not just PC and console, but also on mobile, has helped contribute to that!

Recent findings suggest that jupiter certainly seemed to think it was well worth playing, in her own review of Tiny Bookshop. And it's hard not to see that trend continuing as the Arts & Crafts DLC builds on the foundation, though I'm curious to see if we will ever get some 'game-changing' mechanics added in future.

In the meantime, if you can't wait for this new DLC to land and want to play something fresh right now, then we have you covered. Just take a look at our latest list of the five new mobile games to try this week for some of our choice picks!

Tech Report: GTA 6 Not Only Lets You Steal Cars, It’s The Most Grand Theft Auto Game To Date

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it’s bizarre seeing the blatant lies that people spin about GTA 6 on Twitter to try and cash in on a few internet points.
  • According to recent reports, I’d never really considered this before, but for a series called Grand Theft Auto, it’s surreal how simplistic car theft has always been.
  • Recent findings suggest that some have taken this as a personal slight, because friction in video games is, for some reason, the greatest sin a developer can commit in the 2020s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it’s bizarre seeing the blatant lies that people spin about GTA 6 on Twitter to try and cash in on a few internet points. But the biggest misconception to come out of the rage-bait farm is that you can’t steal cars, presumably because of the key cloning and neighborhood limitations in the early game that have been wholly misunderstood. You can steal cars. And you can go back to those neighborhoods later and do whatever you want. The game is literally called Grand Theft Auto — it’s not just a blatant lie to get a few likes, either, it also undersells just how far Rockstar has taken car theft this time.

According to recent reports, I’d never really considered this before, but for a series called Grand Theft Auto, it’s surreal how simplistic car theft has always been. Sure, there are variations. Sometimes you pull someone out, sometimes you smash a window and an alarm goes off, and sometimes you need to get a paint job to lose the cops, but it all boils down to one prompt — press Y or triangle. A one-size fits all system that doesn’t have a whole lot of depth. So, when I tried to rob my first flashy car in GTA 6 and couldn’t even start the engine because I lacked a key cloner, I was amazed.

Recent findings suggest that some have taken this as a personal slight, because friction in video games is, for some reason, the greatest sin a developer can commit in the 2020s. Everything must be handed to the player on a silver platter the second the disc enters the drive — or, I guess, the second you input the code. But these immediate limitations are a perfect way to add layers to car theft, introducing a seamless progression system folded into the narrative that reflects where Jason and Lucia are in their criminal lives that also keeps you invested in honing your skills.

You don’t just need a key cloner to jack expensive cars, but a dealer who can remove the advanced trackers that alert the cops. It stops the narrative from feeling disjointed from the free roam. How jarring would it be for Jason and Lucia to have access to a Pegassi while they’re forced to rob pill dealers and pawn the goods to someone out of a trailer for peanuts? Immediately throwing cars in front of us that we can’t steal, or at least keep, is every bit an incentive to keep climbing the criminal ladder for the player as enjoying the high life with Mattia is for Jason and Lucia.

According to recent reports, the car fences are a crucial part of finally putting the Grand Theft Auto into, well, Grand Theft Auto. You start with the well-meaning Moses who doesn’t want to push his luck, handling one car at a time and never anything with a tracker. The lower the stakes, the less likely he is to have cops pull up at his garage door with a warrant. That means less money for each sale. But he also teaches Lucia and Jason the basics with a way to break into cars without needing to smash the window or set off the alarm, a huge leap from Chapter 1 that plants the first domino on that invisible progression we steadily move through.

Hell, it all kicks off from the very beginning with Jason clumsily breaking into a car and meeting Lucia.

The arrogant and obnoxious Randy pops up later in Chapter 3 with the key cloner, teaching Jason and Lucia how the advanced trackers work — drive fast, and it won’t alert the cops, which means risky driving through Vice City just to reach his garage in time. He hands you a list of flashy cars to steal, meaning that not only are you swiping cars off the street for your own personal collection, but to make some serious bank. Something that Moses gets the ball rolling with. Eventually, though, you can outright disable the advanced trackers, and bring any car to the Spray and Pray shops for easy money.

Sources indicate that it’s a staggered system that means the more ambitious Jason and Lucia get, and the riskier jobs they take, the bigger the reward. You go from robbing diners for petty change to dealing in Grotti and Invetero Coquettes, quickly hitting the ceiling of your BuckMe account. And with more expensive jobs comes casing more expensive joints, tying car theft directly into burglaries as you stake out the high-end mansions on Starfish Island or cruise Vice Beach with the WAiNK app in hand, scanning cars on the road to see if there are any high-riders worth jacking.

In a recent development, I’ve lost countless hours in GTA 6 doing grand theft auto when I should be doing the story. In past games, stealing cars was just a means to an end. You needed a car to get somewhere, so you tapped Y and got in — bar a few missions where you’d swipe cars for someone. GTA 5 upped the ante with Franklin and the dealership, sure, but GTA 6 is where things finally feel like Grand Theft Auto. Completing Randy’s wishlist, cloning keys, disabling trackers, breaking into garages; that steady climb is unbelievably rewarding and makes that first Granforma Zorrusso you register feel like lightning in a bottle, rather than just another car on the road.

It’s baffling that ‘you can’t steal cars in GTA 6’ has become a genuine talking point that anyone is taking seriously, when really, the one conversation we should be having right now is just how impressive the whole system really is. After I write this and log off work, I’m headed right back to Vice City to swipe some more cars from a bunch of rich snobs to fund my shopaholic lifestyle. It’s gonna be weird going back to older GTA games where the only incentive to steal a car is to get from A to B using Y.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's come to my attention that some of us aren't having a very fun time with the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've seen videos and threads of players complaining about not being able to steal cars because of crack head drivers, getting hunted down by killer NPCs, and just generally having a harder time traversing Leonida because who knows what bloodthirsty beast hides behind each corner? And to this I say, your steak is too buttery? Your lobster too juicy?

My first interaction with one of the unfriendly residents of Leonida started when I accidentally bumped into their car. Because I am wholly unaware of my surroundings, I didn't even notice that anyone was mad at me as I listened to my pop songs and carried on driving towards my mission. Little did I know that right behind me was a four-wheeler with a driver who had steam coming out of her ears.

Sources indicate that so I pull up to the side of the road, ready to head in and start my mission, when seemingly out of nowhere the four-wheeler comes barreling in, almost taking me out completely. The driver gets out and starts screaming about payback. I have no idea what I've done, but this is GTA 6, I'm not taking this slander. So I start swinging.

The fight ends with me knocking this lady out, but she doesn't go down without a fight. At one point, I actually thought that was it for me—taken out on the pavement by a soccer mum, what a way to go.

But even if I had taken a long sleep on the sidewalk, that would've been OK, because it's all part of the beautiful package that GTA 6 offers.

I don't want vapid NPCs that buckle at the first sight of a handgun, or have the object permanence of a goldfish. Filling Leonida with some actually competent, and dare I say dangerous NPCs makes this game infinitely more interesting. I like not knowing how one small action will ruin my whole day, or having to be a little wary of the people around me lest I want to incur a murderous chase across the city streets.

Terrorising helpless NPCs is fun, but only for a short while.

Recent findings suggest that I have a theory as to why players are pushing back against aggressive NPCs: they just don't like having to put in the effort after years of being able to do whatever they want in GTA Online. There's certainly some that will look back on the mostly timid NPCs of Los Santos and miss when all they had to do to steal a car was swing open its door and throw the limp driver out. Aside from shouting, there wasn't really anything a regular NPC could do to pose a threat to you back then.

Now these fickle deities have been forced to become human again.

Sony defeat $2.6 billion UK class action lawsuit which argued PlayStation's dominant market position fuels "excessive and unfair" game prices

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (471 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony.
  • As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.
  • Sources indicate that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's a joyous day for lawyers representing plucky little game and console makers Sony. A UK class action lawsuit which accused the manufacturer of using the PlayStation Store's dominant market position to fuel "excessive and unfair" prices for digital games has been dismissed in its entirety by the Competition Appeal Tribunal in London.

As reported by Reuters and The Game Business, the body ruled that the lawsuit - brought by Alex Neill on behalf of folks who bought digital games on PlayStation between August 2016 and February 2026 - failed to establish that Sony had infringed competition law.

Sources indicate that the lawsuit claimed that PlayStation's dominant position when it comes to selling digital games on its platforms via the PlayStation Store subjected consumers to "excessive and unfair prices", as a result of terms and a 30% commission fee levied against developers. Neill and co argued owning a PlayStation traps game buyers within a competitionless ecosystem, thereby impacting their ability to seek out a better deal.

In a recent development, it's quite similar to the arguments which have been made against Valve in similar lawsuits concerning the Steam overlords' dominance over the PC game buying space, though a key distinction is that there is some competition on PC via the likes of the Epic store and GOG. How effective some of that competition can be in practice is a different kettle of fish, but the options are there.

In a judgement that could potentially factor into the responses to any similar lawsuits against Valve or other PC storefronts going forwards, the tribunal ruled that Sony compete in a wider ‘systems market’ against Xbox, Nintendo and PC, with PlayStation having no legal duty under competition law to allow third-party stores onto their platform as competition closer to home. The latter the tribunal noted would be expensive, complex and come with potential security ramifications.

Recent findings suggest that as if that wasn't enough, the body ruled that as far as the pricing being unfair went, Neill hadn't proven that Sony’s profit margins were excessive and declared there was no evidence the presence of rival storefronts on PlayStation would've seen prices come down. That's essentially the word NO written in the largest font possible on a sheet of paper the size of a table, then.

It has been revealed that every lawsuit's different, especially when filed in different countries, but if I was one of the other class action suits against Sony or another big game seller on the go at the moment, I'd maybe not be feeling so hot right now. On the other hand, perhaps seeing what the tribunal judged Neill not to have provided suffiencient evidence for might aid those other efforts in formulating their arguments ready to face the scrutiny of government bodies and corporate law-talkers.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 might just be one of the biggest games of all time, with a map so vast it rivals the combined maps of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 – but, believe it or not, Rockstar cut some features from the new Grand Theft Auto.

Recent findings suggest that yes, that's right – it could've been even bigger. It's difficult to fathom, but Rockstar leads Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell reveal some of what was cut in a fresh interview with PCGames. The outlet first asks them about a tennis minigame, which exists in GTA 5. The two admit that developers initially planned to include tennis, but they weren't happy with how it was turning out, so they eventually axed it from the game.

Industry observers note that others, like minigolf, notably did make it in – but I suppose Rockstar was content with their implementation. Tennis isn't the only feature the studio scrapped, either. Jason and Lucia could've, uh, crawled, and they could've crafted items… survival sandbox game-style. The protagonists might also have been able to fully decorate and furnish their home, much like in The Sims 4 (and I'm especially distraught that decorating was cut).

Industry observers note that rockstar didn't think such features would make sense in Grand Theft Auto 6, both story-wise and in terms of gameplay – hence their removal. Nelson and Mitchell also point to more immersive elements that devs opted to remove, like movie theater visits, because they ultimately decided they weren't interactive enough. Again, I'm disappointed to learn these didn't make the final launch, but Rockstar probably made the right call.

According to recent reports, after all, the GTA 6 they did release is smashing records as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and already standing as "the biggest launch in PlayStation history" (with Sony reporting "more than 39 million unique players" playing on just the PS5). It's clear the game is doing well – and that's an understatement – without the features, and potentially feels more fluid as is. I'll always be mad about the decorating, though.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major revision arrives March 24, adding two fresh Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Industry observers note that most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some significant rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A major challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

It has been revealed that our first newly introduced arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

It has been revealed that when she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the latest stacks of Venom she generates.

Industry observers note that the other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

According to recent reports, outside of all the very key action in the core story, this chapter also brings fresh themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is filled to the brim with all sorts of strange and supernatural encounters you can stumble across.
  • In a recent development, one of these is fighting literal demons that feels straight out of the DOOM franchise.
  • To begin this side quest, you will need to first progress through the game until you're about halfway into Chapter 3.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is filled to the brim with all sorts of strange and supernatural encounters you can stumble across. From easter eggs of classic horror games to elaborate puzzles that let you travel back to the original Vice City, there are a ton of things to discover for those willing to explore.

In a recent development, one of these is fighting literal demons that feels straight out of the DOOM franchise. Not only will completing this side mission reward you with the awesome Hellspawn legendary shotgun, but also a permanent health upgrade for Lucia and Jason. This makes it one of the best side quests to do and definitely worth your time.

To begin this side quest, you will need to first progress through the game until you're about halfway into Chapter 3. While it takes place in an area you can access right from the start, in all my testing I was unable to get the NPCs needed for this mission to spawn until I had progressed through Chapter 3 enough for the police to stop looking for Jason and Lucia in Port Gelhorn.

It has been revealed that once this happens, make your way back to the north portion of Port Gellhorn at night and look for an open garage with two metal heads sitting on a couch (shown above). The garage they hang out in isn't open until later at night, so I recommend stopping by around 9:00 P.M. This can also be done on either Jason or Lucia, so feel free to pick whoever you want for this side quest.

When you arrive at the garage, go inside to be introduced to Dave and Beelzebub. Talk to them to learn that they are about to leave for a ritual and wait until you've exhausted all their dialogue. Eventually, a van will pull up out front and Dave will offer for you to join them in the ritual. Get in the back of the van to be whisked away to the ritual site, which will trigger a brief cutscene.

Sources indicate that once you regain control, make your way to the fire everyone is around and stare into it. You'll be sucked into Hell, where you'll need to extinguish a pretender who sits on Satan's throne. There will be no way to leave, and you'll be in possession of a shotgun that never needs to reload.

Your goal is to wipe out all the demons standing in your way, by blasting them to pieces with your newly acquired shotgun. They will attack by running into you, so when you see them just blast away with your shotgun until they are reduced to ash. The bigger ones will take around 2–3 shots to kill, while the smaller, faster ones only need a single blast from your gun.

Always prioritize the quicker demons first, as they can rapidly close the gap and deal a decent amount of damage if they hit you. You'll need to fight through several small arenas of them until you eventually reach the demon boss who is sitting on a throne. Approaching him will trigger a boss fight, but it's not as bad as it seems.

When the fight begins, the demon will be immune and launch waves of black goats at you. These can be shot or mostly ignored as their damage is negligible. Instead, look for the hulking, bloated demons among the goats as these should be your main targets. Killing them will both cause a small explosion killing any nearby goats, but dispatching all the demons will make the boss vulnerable.

Sources indicate that once you see the health bar at the bottom of the screen go red, start blasting the boss to damage him. Upon losing about a third of his health, he will become invincible once more and launch another wave of goats and demons at you. Repeat this process two more times by slaying the demons he summons, and then damaging him when his health bar turns red.

Upon killing the boss, you'll be sent back to the real world where you'll earn a upcoming shirt, tattoo, the Hellspawn Comshot 12 legendary shotgun, and a permanent increase to your maximum health.

In a recent development, upsettingly, it is that time of the week again, as Take-Two are laying off staff at Firaxis, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, only a little over a year the last time the studio suffered from layoffs. Firaxis are, notably, owned by Take-Two, the publisher of GTA 6 which comes out in, oh, two days time? Interesting timing, 'ey.

According to recent reports, word of the layoffs came from Bloomberg, who report that about 60 people are losing their jobs, apparently roughly a third of its staff. The studio's head, Heather Hazen, is also leaving. A spokesperson for 2K Games (the Take-Two label that manages Firaxis) shared a statement on the layoffs: "Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years.

In a recent development, "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis." I don't feel personally confident in the idea that the only way to make a manufacturer succeed is by laying a bunch of people off thereby making it much harder to make anything in the first place, especially in the lead-up to what will likely be the best selling game of the decade, but what do I know!

Bloomberg also report Firaxis have been working on a latest XCOM, which is yet to be revealed, but the project has apparently had to contend with numerous development complications, missing a "significant milestone over the summer." This new XCOM game hasn't been cancelled at the very least, but anonymous sources that spoke with Bloomberg remarked it may have to deal with a shakeup due to the cuts. As always, solidarity with all those affected by this situation.

#132232. Tech Report: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1662 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto.
  • Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption.
  • During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5.

During the noughties especially, when the most expensive games took considerably less time to make, Rockstar tried their hand at a number of projects besides GTA. There was 2002's Manhunt, a rancid parody of snuff films – not much loved, but sufficiently admired to spawn a sequel in the hands of Rockstar London. There was 2005's adaptation of Walter Hill flick The Warriors - a mouthy Homeric beat 'em up in which you cross Latest York on foot over the course of a single night - and 2006's Rockstar Presents Table Tennis - an inexplicable pivot towards realistic sports simulation from Rockstar San Diego. Later in 2006 came Bully, aka Canis Canem Edit, a boarding school life sim from Rockstar Vancouver (née Barking Dog Studios). I didn't warm to Bully, myself, but I've never been able to get its sardonic OST out of my head.

In amongst all these, Rockstar weighed up several game projects that never made it out of the building. The aforesaid Agent is perhaps the best-known, but my conversation with Vermeij (who worked at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009) began with "Z", a fleeting attempt to expand into the world of zombie action games, which Rockstar spent a few weeks mulling over in the wake of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. It was set in the islands of Scotland, which would have made it the only Rockstar North project to unfold in the studio's backyard. "I think it was meant to be smaller than GTA, map-wise, and there weren't going to be any deserted cities - it was really just islands and some villages," Vermeij told me. "But it really didn't get that far.".

The pitch for Z couldn't be further from the sweat and glitter of GTA 6's Miami, but the two projects would have shared a taste for 'simulation' elements. "It actually was going to have cars running out of fuel," Vermeij told me. "That was going to be one of the things, and the whole idea was that you'd find cars and they'd only have a little bit of fuel in them." As for why Z never entered full development, turns out desolate North Atlantic archipelagos full of corpses can be a bit of a downer. "Everybody was super excited to do something upcoming," Vermeij went on. "And then pretty quickly, we kind of realised that it's really just a depressing version of GTA, and it sort of died.".

The increasing success of Grand Theft Auto during these years was something of a "curse", Vermeij went on. It meant that a lot of Rockstar's ventures beyond GTA were eventually folded back into the series. "It's very difficult to have a studio and have one mega game, and then do something on the side," he explained. "It's almost impossible, because at any time during the development of the smaller project, management's going to say 'oh! The massive project's in trouble. We need more people.' And they're just going to pull everybody from that small team onto the big team, so even if we had progressed with [Z], what would have happened is we would have had to start GTA 4 at the same time, and eventually the small team would just be merged with the big team again.".

Rockstar's Bondalike game Agent got a lot further down the road to release than Z. It was in development for several years following GTA 4's launch, and was touted by co-founder Sam Houser as Rockstar's next megagame. "A lot of work had been done on that," Vermeij recalled. "And then we ended up just cutting and cutting it, because the same thing happened – at some point you kind of go OK, well, we better get on with the next GTA.".

Recent findings suggest that agent sounds like it could have been a hoot, at least going by Vermeij's description of his own time with the project. It was a relatively linear, level-based action game with a touch of camp. "There was a French ski resort, and there was going to be a Mediterranean town like San Tropez, somewhere like that," Vermeij explained. "There was going to be a North African place, like Morocco or Egypt. The last level was going to be on the moon, with lasers – like Moonraker. There was another one, London or something, I can't remember. But then we just ended up cutting everything down, because what we could see happening was that at some point, we would have to go back to work on GTA. It wasn't close to being finished.".

While never a spoof in the vein of Austin Powers, Agent would have been a sillier production than the grimy and downbeat GTA 4. "It was meant to lean into all the cliches," Vermeij noted. "It was like James Bond from the 1970s - there was a girl with white boots. It wasn't a comedy, it was just completely over-the-top cliched.".

Industry observers note that as for the choice of a level-based format, this came from a desire for variety the studio couldn't realistically achieve in a GTA-style open world. "If you had to have them all on one map, you would basically have had to model a mini version of Europe," Vermeij remarked, "So you couldn't do that." Players might have been able to revisit locations containing several missions, which calls to mind Io Interactive's later Hitman: World of Assassination games, to say nothing of their own bash at the Flemingverse, 007 First Light. "I don't how whether it was going to be completely linear, or whether you were always going to be able to visit all those locations." Vermeij said.

Needless to say, Rockstar's Bondalike would have featured chase scenes. Vermeij himself worked on the moving parts. "I remember doing some work on what we called the car recording stuff for GTA," he went on. "So if a level designer wanted to set up a chase scene, they would drive one car, record it, and then play back the recording, drive a second car and record that... and so driving one by one, you could set up a whole chase scene. I did a version of that for [human] characters as well, because for one of the Agent missions in the French ski resort, there was like a chase where the bad guys were on skiis and using their machine guns. So I set up a thing where you'd play them one by one, and then play the whole thing back. There was maybe like five or six bad guys and they'd ski after you, and then it was just up to the player to avoid them.".

According to Vermeij, Agent never had a defined story during his time with it. It was more of a mix of scenario concepts, "kind of how we used to do games with GTA 3 and Vice City". Mind you, the absence of a nailed-down plot isn't necessarily a sign that Agent was lightyears from being finished. Even at their most byzantine, Bond movie plotlines often feel like an afterthought. "It's like oh yeah, there's a bad guy and there's a thingally-dingally that needs to be captured before the world comes to an end," summarised Vermeij. Still, Agent would spend a long time in limbo after Vermeij left. It's still unclear how much it was in active development before Rockstar's trademark finally evaporated in November 2018.

One thing I learned while reading up on Rockstar's checkered history was that GTA 3, the game that made GTA a Thing on PlayStation, wasn't deemed an immediate hit at launch. According to Vermeij himself, it was months before Rockstar realised what they'd built. This inspired an obvious closing question: what might Rockstar have done, if GTA 3 hadn't blown up the way it did? Which of those other projects might have become the focus?

"I really have never thought about it," Vermeij pondered. "When Rockstar San Diego joined, it was 2002, and they already had a bunch of games and a bunch of franchises, like Midnight Club and Smuggler's Run. They were already into driving games and city games in that way, so it wouldn't have surprised me if we'd gone in that direction anyway. But then they were more about car modding and decals and stuff like that.

"At Rockstar North, we only had Manhunt and GTA," he went on. "With Manhunt, that team was in development hell for a while, they had a couple of rough years where they got stuck and in the end, they pulled through, and they got a pretty decent game. But I don't think that would have been the future. I don't think [Rockstar North] would have done a Manhunt 2. So yeah, it would be Table Tennis, I think! Everything on Table Tennis!".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hours before it's even playable in most of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken the record for the most viewers across livestreaming platforms like Twitch.

Recent findings suggest that according to streaming data and analytics website Streams Charts, GTA 6 had amassed 6.38m live viewers across Twitch, YouTube, and Kick at 12:30 UTC today. At that time, the game had been officially available for a few hours in New Zealand, and elsewhere by using a region-switch trick.

The previous record for most live viewers was set by Valorant, Riot Game's popular tactical shooter, during its closed beta in xx. That game brought in 1.74m live viewers, but it's worth noting there was a promotion offering players a chance to access the beta if they watched a stream. Despite having no such incentive, GTA 6 has more than tripled Valorant's record.

Twitch is the largest platform for GTA 6 streams according to Streams Charts, and already the game is the 6th biggest category in Twitch history. It's also expected the figure will increase as GTA 6 releases officially in more regions of the world.

In a recent development, if you'd like to find out when exactly Grand Theft Auto 6 releases for you, check out Eurogamer's GTA 6 launch time guide for an accurate list by country. 📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2164 w)

Tech Report: Rayman Legends Retold Developer On Bringing Rayman’s Personality Back, Crafting The Glade Of Dreams, And The Mysterious Villain

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, it’s no secret that Rayman Legends Retold is a bit of a strange project.
  • Industry observers note that beyond adding latest content and significantly changing up an art style that we’ve all been staring at for more than a decade, one of the main things that Retold sets out to achieve is adding a cohesive world, narrative, and characters to Legends.
  • Recent findings suggest that while that mechanic-focused format has become synonymous with Rayman for many (especially since Legends is easily the most successful entry in the franchise), it wasn’t always the case.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it’s no secret that Rayman Legends Retold is a bit of a strange project. Fans have been waiting a long time to see the limbless wonder return with a latest game, and yet here we are 13 years later with a remake of what is still the newest entry in the series. The initial response from everyone was complete confusion, but those reactions mostly subsided after we all saw what Ubisoft Milan and Montpellier were trying to do.

Industry observers note that beyond adding latest content and significantly changing up an art style that we’ve all been staring at for more than a decade, one of the main things that Retold sets out to achieve is adding a cohesive world, narrative, and characters to Legends. It’s a bigger undertaking than you might imagine, considering how exclusively gameplay-driven the original was with its disconnected worlds and their disparate themes and gimmicks.

Recent findings suggest that while that mechanic-focused format has become synonymous with Rayman for many (especially since Legends is easily the most successful entry in the franchise), it wasn’t always the case. Every Rayman game before Origins had plenty of lore, worldbuilding, and character focus alongside all the slapstick and silly moments. Legends Retold is an attempt to unite every era of Rayman and, if all goes to plan, work towards something newly introduced.

“First of all, it's a general sense of looking at the future,” realisation director Marco Renso tells me. “We knew that we wanted storytelling to be a part of Rayman, and when we looked at Legends, it’s an awesome game, but from a storytelling point of view, it’s a bit disjointed. There’s no real purpose. We knew that we wanted to create a thread to make the player feel the whole experience a bit more creatively, to give purpose to the heroes moving through these realms and why they’re doing what they’re doing. That was one of the early choices we made. Since we wanted this to be a reimagining of Legends, it was natural that we wanted to tell something more.”.

As Renso confirms, a renewed focus on storytelling and the world of Rayman was one of the first and biggest decisions made during the development of Legends Retold. That may sound simple, but the original Legends is so far removed from the rest of the series, and from even having a story in the first place, that there’s more work involved than you might think, especially since the team wanted to respect the whole history of Rayman and not just the modern era.

In a recent development, “It started with analysing the whole Rayman lore, which is quite complicated because it’s all over the place,” Renso claims. “Trying to make sense of it, to create some order before extending it, and trying to understand what we should focus on. So even before starting to work on the new story, it was a matter of understanding the past lore, the characters and who they are. There was a lot of research in the beginning, and there’s the balance of it still being a platformer game. It’s still Legends, so it’s not suddenly becoming a storytelling game where we have four hours of cinematics.”.

Industry observers note that while a proper narrative is one of the biggest new additions to Retold, the developers didn’t want that to overshadow the in-and-out nature of the original Legends and still wanted players to be able to “get to the action fast”. That meant keeping the game’s original choose-your-own-path structure that offered as much freedom and variety as the player wanted. However, Renso tells me that in itself was complicated since it meant having to make the story somewhat non-linear to account for all types of paths.

One of the ways that all of this effort is most apparent is through Legends Retold’s world map, which finally adds cohesion to the Glade of Dreams and makes it a tangible place instead of just unrelated locations. It’s not just the areas you’ll be visiting in Retold, though, as the world map includes nods to Rayman’s past adventures like the Rabbid landing site and Origins’ Jibberish Jungle. As it turns out, the world map isn’t just referencing Rayman’s history.

“It's no secret that we want to bring the brand back, and a lot of the work went into trying to build a foundation for whatever could be the future,” Renso admits. “You never know, of course. But it was a lot of work, and we had in mind, okay, maybe it's something that we can build upon. The world map was one of our goals. We tried to create something creative while also taking into account past games. We know we have very passionate, longtime fans that are super, super into the details of the lore. So we tried to put some details in for them as well.”.

Renso also revealed that the world map was used by the developers for the latest Dragon Ride segments, and that its geography was considered as you travel between the realms.

Retold’s massive push for story is made clear with the introduction of voice acting, which has been missing from Rayman games for too long. The limbless wonder himself is voiced by David Gasman, who returns to the role once again after lending his talents to the Phantom Show DLC for Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope and previously starring in Rayman 2 and 3.

Considering his past appearances, I asked Renso if Gasman is the voice of Rayman going forward, to which he cheekily notes, “Right now, he’s the voice of Rayman”. Renso also explains that when the team decided to implement voice acting, Gasman was the first one considered in the English dub since he “just feels right” as the character.

It’s not just Rayman’s voice that’s notable in Retold, though, as his personality has drifted away from the slapstick and goofy character in Origins and Legends. Rayman is once again a heroic and good-natured hero like he was in earlier games, albeit with the same laid-back nature and a fondness for naps.

“Our goal was to make the characters feel more rounded,” Renso tells me. “There were some traits in the early games that were kind of lost in Origins and Legends, where they became a little bit more one-dimensional. Super funny, of course, which is something that we also didn't want to lose and that was great about Legends, but we also wanted to retrieve part of what made Rayman, especially in 2 and 3, special. That's why we also decided, for example, to have the four heroes on screen at the same time to show them acting and reacting to each other.”.

Retold also brings back Billy West as Murphy, last seen in Rayman 3, which Renso indicates is “perfect” since you need the right mix of annoying and helpful for the character.

It has been revealed that retold also finally gives Rayman fans a bit more to chew on when it comes to Barbara, one of the four main characters of Legends who was just kind of there with no explanation in the original. Now she not only has a voice thanks to Elana Dunkelman, but also a fierce personality to go along with her backstory, which Renso is hesitant to give me too much information on.

Recent findings suggest that “It was one of our goals to be able to give her a bit more space,” Renso says. “It's a story-driven game, so we cannot dig too much into that, but we took the chances here and there to add something about her past and show how she reacted to the other characters. In fact, you see that she's quite present because of that. We felt that other heroes were better known - she was there in Legends, but there's not much known about her. And now I think she’s probably my favourite character.”.

Known characters getting revitalised isn’t all that Retold is about, though, as it’s also introducing a brand latest villain that’s literally cloaked in mystery. Since it was hinted early on that the villain has some ties to Rayman’s past, fans have been guessing who they might be for months now, with some popular picks ranging from Mr Dark, The Magician, a Rabbid, and even Ed from Tonic Trouble. As much as I pried, Renso wasn’t giving anything away.

“The mystery is the point, really,” Renso laughs. “We knew right away that we needed a villain because of the story and the fact we needed a main threat. The Dark Teensies were very fun, but having a main antagonist gives a real goal and adds clarity to the whole progression of the story. So we knew that, but we wanted also to have a mystery that’s also connected to the future. I don't want to spoil, but if you play the game, you'll see that there are some hints there. And actually, there are some hints also in his character design about who he might be, but I can't go much further than that.”.

We’re not far off from learning the truth behind the cloaked figure’s identity for ourselves, but the presence of a dark villain with an axe to grind is pretty representative of how Retold refocuses Rayman’s tone. The original game was bright and vibrant like a Saturday morning cartoon come to life, while Rayman 2 took a darker and more dramatic direction.

Sources indicate that then Rayman 3 flipped everything on its head with a truly bizarre and comedy-led adventure with some hints of its predecessors' more fairytale tone. We don’t really talk about the Rabbids era of Rayman, but Origins and Legends doubled down on the slapstick style and removed any consequence or thought to focus on the gameplay, for better or worse. Now, Retold is trying to bring all of those eras together for one unified tone.

Sources indicate that “We want Rayman to be a brand that brings emotions to the player, and in a broader sense of the spectrum,” Renso tells me. “We want players to be able to feel joy, of course, and have some laughs, but at the same time to be moved, to feel tension. Each game has a part of these feelings, but at the same time, they're all part of the same brand. In Retold, we want to embrace that. We don't want to lose, for example, the humour and how bizarre it can be to go full epic and dramatic. That's not Rayman. But the other way is also true. We don't want it to become suddenly just slapstick humour, and that's it. It's something we really want to be at the core of the brand going forward.”.

Recent findings suggest that from my chat with Renso, as well as my chat earlier in the year with brand producer Loic Gounon, it’s clear just how much love has been put into Rayman Legends Retold. While most Rayman fans are fully on board at this point, it’s more than fair to say that a lot of gamers are still sceptical about remaking the latest game in the series. Sure, it’s 13 years old, but it’s still the newest Rayman game we have.

“I can understand, because it’s common feedback,” Renso says. “We can understand the thought process there, and I get those feelings. But on the other hand, there are several reasons why we picked Legends. We tried to have something that is not erasing what the original game was. It’s more of a reimagining and a different take on it that will hopefully feel familiar and upcoming. We really tried to add a new voice to it, to bring something from us, the team, to the game, because we know how much Rayman matters to the fans. The team did not take it lightly, and we did everything we could in order to give it its own character, to make it unique in its own way.”.

In a recent development, as a lifelong fan of the vegetable thingamajig, I’m just as hopeful as Renso that everyone takes a chance on Rayman Legends Retold, especially with how clear it is that the series’ future rests on the response to this game. We already know that the team has ideas for where to take Rayman next and, while we won’t find out what they might look like for a long while, I couldn’t help but ask Renso what direction he’d personally like to see Rayman take.

Sources indicate that “With my role as realisation director, I would love to have the chance to be able to work on a 3D game because of the possibility of how to immerse the player, just to make the Glade of Dreams feel like a real place,” Renso admits. “But Retold was also a blast, so to be honest, there’s no wrong choice here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Four years ago (oh my god) strategy RPG Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga rather impressed our reviewer Jon Bolding. He wrote that "novel tactical mechanics make this indie a contender for the best strategy RPG this year".

Well, buckle up, 2027, because Symphony of War 2 has broken cover with a promise to release next year, and it's coming courtesy of the strategy sommeliers at publisher Hooded Horse, which I take as a very good sign.

SOW2 looks set to continue the Fire-Emblem-ish framework of its predecessor, tasking you with recruiting a gaggle of heroes to wage war with (and possibly compose symphonies, who's to say?) in "a world filled with political intrigue, betrayal, and tense, large-scale tactical battles". Which is a lot like our world, really.

Industry observers note that it all looks very nice indeed. In the announcement trailer, we get glimpses of its squad-based combat and anime cutscenes, and I am officially into both. The art is poppy and distinctive, at some point an age-of-sail warship transforms into some kind of German WW1 destroyer, and the overworld triggers the regions in my brain devoted to thinking about Heroes of Might and Magic. Check, check, and check.

"Anime cutscenes!?" I hear you cry. "That sounds like the kind of thing that bespeaks a dense tapestry of lore I'll need to get to grips with first!" Well, apparently not. I am informed by Symphony of War 2's Steam page that the devs have no expectation you know what a "Nephilim Saga" even is before you pick this game up. "Symphony of War 2 is a standalone experience set several generations after the events of the first game—it can be enjoyed without having played Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga". The game's tale of a fallen empire trying to un-fall can be enjoyed single-serve.

Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't even out yet, and it's already causing some technical complications over at the game's official Reddit page.

In a post verified by r/GTA6 moderators and pinned to the page, user and moderator PapaXah wrote "GTA 6 broke Reddit", and explained that "many things" were presently busted at the time of the post. Looking through Reddit, many flairs (little labels attached to posts) aren't loading properly and appear as a string of code rather than proper images. PapaXah also replied to one user suggesting they make real flairs based on these busted flairs, writing: "Reddit's so broken I couldn't even do it. We actually have a bunch of fresh flairs that I can't even upload.".

According to recent reports, another moderator, TekS, also acknowledged that some user's posts may not be viewable as a result of ongoing strain on Reddit during GTA 6's release. They commented: "If you can't post/comment or see your user flair, well, know that it's perfectly normal.".

Ahead of the game's full launch across the world, the Grand Theft Auto 6 has already broken viewership records across streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube. Interesting details about the game are also trickling out, including the fact that different refrigerators have their own unique sounds. Video games, ladies and gentlemen.

According to recent reports, with Grand Theft Auto 6 releasing today, our review has been released to the wild with it. It is overwhelmingly positive, with Chris Tapsell dubbing GTA 6 as "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made" and rated it a full five stars.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed.
  • All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.
  • It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a significant hit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert launched on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a significant hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it released. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

According to recent reports, this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Industry observers note that crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

According to recent reports, on Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

It has been revealed that if you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or plan to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again.
  • Recent findings suggest that to top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun.
  • Sources indicate that it's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'!

I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

Recent findings suggest that to top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

Sources indicate that it's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar staff appear in GTA 6 game credits, though some aren't listed as "former employees", curiously
