💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, REVISION 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6.
  • Also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know.
  • ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is right now facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, REVISION 19TH NOVEMBER: All of the 34 fired Rockstar employees appear in the credits for GTA 6. We were able to confirm the final few names' existence there after Rockstar posted the full credits online - in searchable form. Before this, the process of cross-checking was intensely laborious: it required watching a scrolling list of names for an hour-and-a-half to see if they appeared.

Also, we couldn't identify six names in the "former employees" section of the credits before because they don't appear there, we now know. These names appear listed under the departments the people worked for, as if they still worked at Rockstar. Why this is, we don't know - perhaps it's something to do with being involved in the employment tribunal or not. We're asking Rockstar for clarification.

ORIGINAL STORY 18TH NOVEMBER: Eurogamer can confirm that at least 28 of the 34 employees fired by Rockstar roughly a year ago - in an action that directly led to the employment tribunal Rockstar is right now facing in Scotland - are named in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6.

We cross-checked a list of 34 names supplied to us by the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain - the same organisation taking action against Rockstar on behalf of the fired employees. And of those names, we found 28 direct matches in the credits, along with a couple of discrepancies we've since verified, and some close-sounding names we're attempting to clarify. Some names may simply be missing. We won't publish the list for privacy reasons.

In a recent development, A number of those fired employees are seeking compensation for unfair dismissal amid allegations of "union busting", in an employment tribunal that comes to an end today. The delayed climax of the case couldn't be more fateful, aligned as it is with tomorrow's release of GTA 6, and the outcome will be historic either way.

Rockstar recently revealed that more than 4,711 people worked at the manufacturer making GTA 6, employed across 12 offices around the world - a staff-count that has more than doubled since Red Dead Redemption 2. It's a game that's wowed critics - Eurogamer awarded GTA 6 five stars in our review this afternoon - and which observers expect to generate $2bn in revenue in its opening weekend alone.

According to recent reports, but perhaps Christian Donlan put it best when digesting the opulence on display in the Netflix 'extended look' GTA 6 trailer. "To spend all this money making something so beautifully rich and detailed, to pay billions for this game and sweat every little animation, to float it out to us on Netflix, amongst genuine discussion around whether Netflix can handle it? That's commitment," he wrote. "And if you're willing to do that, and willing to do that to tell an underdog story, you should let your workers who made everything form a union.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

Sources indicate that today’s revision follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

According to recent reports, the action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

Recent findings suggest that this latest enhancement only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

The most key changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added latest pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6's Ultimate Edition has proven enormously popular, despite its hefty $100 price tag. So much so that Strauss Zelnick, boss of Rockstar parent tech giant Take-Two, recently confirmed it's the edition most people are buying - and that's despite a lack of specific information about how its unlockable content works. With GTA 6 just hours away from release, however - and out now in certain parts of the work - details are beginning to emerge, and the answer is perhaps a little surprising.

As previously confirmed, the $100/£90 Ultimate Edition provides access to exclusive vehicles, weapons, shops, and more, with the full list as follows:.

It has been revealed that rockstar also previously revealed that "Ultimate Edition bonuses become available to Jason and Lucia across their story, with latest items uncovered behind each chapter". The specifics of how - and when - all this stuff unlocks, though, remained unclear. So if you've opted for the Ultimate Edition, you might be wondering where your stuff is when you finally fire up the game. As reported by IGN, which has full unlock details, it turns out virtually all of GTA 6's Ultimate Edition content, as per details in the in-game shop, requires progressing through the main story - in some cases dozens and dozens of hours into the story - before it'll become available.

Recent findings suggest that ultimate Edition-exclusive shops, for instance, unlock during Chapter 1, and many of the other additions become available by the end of Chapter 2. That doesn't sound too difficult, but as Eurogamer's Chris Tapsell notes, reaching that point could take upward of 25 hours. As for some of the late-game unlocks, such as the Shitzu Squalo and the Vice City Style outfits and tattoos (available in Chapter 4) and Chapter 5's 95 Grotti Cheetah, you could be looking at closing in on 60 hours of playtime before they unlock.

"It'll vary depending how hard people focus on the main story," Chris explains, "but if you were mostly focused on the main story plus the optional character-based missions in largely chronological order, that's about how long it'd take.".

It has been revealed that it's also worth noting - perhaps surprisingly - that some Ultimate Edition content is only a temporary unlock, usable only during specific chapters. Jason's Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak, for instance, can only be accessed and enjoyed during Chapter 1. That's also true for his retro Vapid Ganado, available from the Coastal Auto Care mod shop in Key Lento. So basically, you'll want to make the most of these while you can!

All this might be a little disappointing for players who were expecting to be showered with Ultimate Edition spoils from the off (and that they'd be permanent unlocks), but the good news is 60 hours in GTA 6 is far from a chore. As Chris explained in his five star GTA 6 review, Rockstar's latest is an "irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action" that "pushes back the horizon of video games once again".

In a recent development, everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

In a recent development, every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

In a recent development, each of the two upcoming regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

The developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

Rockstar’s IWGB Union Fails By Majority Vote After GTA 6 Release

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The industry-shaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6 has overshadowed just about everything else going on in the gaming world right now, but one area that has suffered the most seems to be the efforts of the union trying to form a partnership with Rockstar's employees.
  • While some developers with the studio have been trying for months or even longer to get the initiative off the ground to protect their employee rights, the latest results shared by the IWGB union on Instagram show that there's still a lot more work to be done.
  • According to reports from sources like the Video Games Chronicle, a vast majority of Rockstar employees voted against the deal that would have seen IWGB representing them as the studio's official union, which turned out to be roughly 75%, or about 1,200 out of the 1,600 employees that participated in the vote against it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The industry-shaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6 has overshadowed just about everything else going on in the gaming world right now, but one area that has suffered the most seems to be the efforts of the union trying to form a partnership with Rockstar's employees.

While some developers with the studio have been trying for months or even longer to get the initiative off the ground to protect their employee rights, the latest results shared by the IWGB union on Instagram show that there's still a lot more work to be done.

According to reports from sources like the Video Games Chronicle, a vast majority of Rockstar employees voted against the deal that would have seen IWGB representing them as the studio's official union, which turned out to be roughly 75%, or about 1,200 out of the 1,600 employees that participated in the vote against it.

While IWGB has had plenty of support leading up to the official vote, which ran from November 12 to November 26, several current Rockstar employees have already been expressing exactly why they think the vote failed, or why they voted no in the first place.

With statements like how "many of us had legitimate concerns that couldn't be answered fully by the IWGB" or dozens of others expressing how their "time at Rockstar has been amazing" with some of the "best working conditions I could possibly dream of," the vote had a lot going against it already.

The main problem many Rockstar employees had with the vote wasn't the concept of a union representing and protecting them itself, but more so the IWGB specifically, which several responses pointed out how they "failed to provide any practical advantages" and made several campaign claims that didn't accurately represent what it was actually like to work at Rockstar during the creation of GTA 6.

The timing of the vote couldn't have been worse either, as while the IWGB was using the release of GTA 6 to provide more attention to their initiative, several Rockstar employees have previously stated they didn't want to take away from the efforts of the developers that worked so hard on the project, or wanted to reap the success of the launch rather than put it at risk over more unsteady union conflicts.

Despite the current results of the vote, however, the IWGB Game Workers union isn't giving up on Rockstar by any means, as they are using the smaller portion of success to "double down" on their efforts and individual representation for Rockstar employees who opt into their organization, as opposed to moving the whole workforce into it.

#132212. Latest Update: I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

Latest Update: I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (888 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop.
  • Sources indicate that many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too rapidly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

Recent findings suggest that if you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Sources indicate that many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The issue is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Recent findings suggest that since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

It has been revealed that when I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a latest paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

Romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

Even the PS5 Pro is "not powerful enough" to run GTA 6 at 60FPS or 40FPS, Rockstar notes

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles.
  • Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.
  • Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, don't expect GTA 6 to get an update supporting higher framerate modes, at least, not on current-generation consoles. Rockstar has explained that even the most powerful console of the bunch, the PS5 Pro, isn't powerful enough to run the lavish game at 40FPS or 60FPS.

Last week, some players weren't too happy with the news that GTA 6 is targeting 30FPS on all platforms it's currently launching on - PS5 Pro, PS5, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. Like countless other massive productions this generation, the hope was that Rockstar Games would offer both quality and performance modes for its lush open-world monster.

Rockstar's now seemingly confirmed that its crime epic won't run at 60FPS or 40FPS anytime soon, simply because it can't on the currently available hardware.

Sources indicate that "While the PS5 Pro's central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game's complex simulation at higher frame rates," the studio's technology production director, Marc Chambers, remarked in a statement to Kotaku. There you have it, then - even the beefiest console around can't handle Leonida at higher framerates.

Chambers did note some of the souped up console's other technical improvements, however: "Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game's visual fidelity.".

The tech gurus over at Digital Foundry gave some more insight into how GTA 6 runs on current-gen machines, calling it a "technical tour de force," though one that can still dip below 30FPS on PS5 and Xbox Series X during busier chase scenes and explosive shootouts. It's perhaps unsurprising, then, that higher framerates are off the table for now.

A 30FPS launch is by no means a departure for Rockstar Games, either. GTA 5 also ran at an unsteady 30FPS when it first dropped onto the Xbox 360 and PS3, with 60FPS support only coming alongside the game's PC port more than a year later. I'm not too fussed about the game's 30FPS target, personally. I'd much rather have a game that consistently hits 30FPS than one that continuously chugs trying to reach 60FPS, especially when it's as frequently drop dead gorgeous as GTA 6.

Industry observers note that the slightly lower framerates haven't affected the game's critical response so far, either. In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, our Chris Tapsell called it a "game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale" as "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again.".

Recent findings suggest that if you're planning to jump into the game at midnight - or if you're virtually travelling to Latest Zealand for early entry - there's a few things to be aware of. First is that you won't be able to replay GTA 6's missions without multiple save files, so be sure to soak it all up. Second, some Ultimate Edition content is only available in the first chapter.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a major expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

It has been revealed that this enhancement will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no upcoming characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other fresh arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Money is more important in Grand Theft Auto 6 than it ever has been before, with Jason and Lucia having countless opportunities to rake in some much-needed dough and make life in Leonida easier.

Sources indicate that just like in GTA 5 and GTA Online, robbing banks is one of the most reliable ways to earn a lot of cash. You won't be able to do so until you unlock a key item, though, so let's get into it.

In a recent development, if you're brave enough to try and rob a bank or any location with Marked Bills in the early hours of GTA 6, you'll very quickly learn that it's a bad idea. In a nice bit of realism, stealing Marked Bills will set off a dye pack when you leave the bank, ruining your entire haul and covering Jason or Lucia in paint.

Thankfully, there's a way to bypass those annoying dye packs and make robbing banks a viable opportunity. To do so, you'll need to unlock the Dye Pack Jammer, a key item that does exactly what it says on the tin and prevents dye packs from exploding. The Dye Pack Jammer is unlocked during the Credit Check story mission in Chapter 3, which means it's unmissable if you put enough time in.

In a recent development, chapter 3 is one of GTA 6's longer acts, and it took me around 40 hours to reach Credit Check. Your mileage will vary depending on how fast you're taking things, however.

According to recent reports, credit Check sees Jason and Lucia being tested on their robbing ability and tasked with hitting up a few different locations. It's one of the game's best missions and, once you've beaten it, you'll be able to steal from any location on the map. In fact, the map will even point this out to you by highlighting a bunch of newly introduced opportunities and pointing you in their direction.

Industry observers note that it's worth noting, however, that any location with Marked Bills will have higher security and will need to be more carefully planned. The pay day is usually worth it, but just keep that in mind.

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (438 w)

Tech Report: GTA 6 won't let you use cheats until you complete the main story, and locks progression when you do

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (438 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.
  • That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2.
  • In a recent development, in GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Here's a twist: you can't use cheats in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you complete the entire game's main story.

That's what we discovered from our tests at least, after loading in saves at various points through the game to be sure, and it's also both a first for the series and a departure even from how developer Rockstar handled cheats in Red Dead Redemption 2. In that game,approximately half of the cheats were available from the off, and the other half required discovering specific newspapers from around the game's world to unlock.

In a recent development, in GTA 6, you'll again need to do some legwork. This time it appears that all of the game's cheats not only require you to finish the story, but also complete various tasks or challenges to unlock them.

The way it works is simple enough. Once you finish the main story, the "Cheats" tab - previously hidden - quietly appears at the far end of the Progress menu, accessible when you open the in-game map and scroll with the bumper buttons. From there, you can view various sub-sections of cheats, sorted by category, and a list of 10 or so cheats for each.

With each cheat there'll be a short explanation of what it does, and what's required to unlock it and, once unlocked, guidance on how to perform it. This is done via whipping out your phone, holding down the shoulder buttons and using various D-Pad inputs - much the same as GTA 5.

There's also another caveat to bear in mind: when you use a cheat, you'll see a notification warning you that the game can't be saved while it's active, and that Trophies and Achievements are also disabled until you end that session. This makes sense, once you understand the nature of GTA 6's story - there is a cheat for giving yourself a load of money, for instance; another departure from GTA 5 where that popular cheat was removed - but given you'll need certain amounts of cash at various points of the story, enabling you to shortcut that would disrupt the way the narrative unfolds.

According to recent reports, we'll have a guide from yours truly to all the game's cheats live on Eurogamer in the very near future, as the game releases here in the UK. In the meantime, if you find yourself on the fence about this one, be sure to give our GTA 6 review a look. As I put it there, giving the game five stars: it is "the most believable and unbelievable video game world ever made".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

It has been revealed that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely newly introduced modes, the possibilities are vast.".

In a recent development, the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a substantial visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, newly introduced motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

In a recent development, beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one massive enhancement sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

Sources indicate that when it was announced that Robert Pattinson had been cast as James Bond, Twilight fans everywhere did a little cheer. Especially if you were Team Edward! What a good long-term investment that’s turned out to be! However, the most popular Twilight-related reaction to Pattinson being 007 stems from the fact that the iconic spy was brought up in the vampire movie. As it turns out, there’s a whole newly introduced layer to that scene we didn’t know about.

Industry observers note that first off, in case you missed it, James Bond is brought up around 58 minutes into 2008’s Twilight. Just seconds before Edward Cullen and Bella Swan make their grand entrance as a couple for the first time at school, one of their classmates, Eric, hands out flyers for the upcoming prom, which is a Monte Carlo theme. Check out the scene below:.

Twilight literally predicted Robert Pattinson being James Bond btw https://t.co/eMfeaVhbhuNovember 16, 2026.

It has been revealed that isn’t that wild? James Bond is literally said in Twilight right before the current James Bond appears. However, there’s more to it. The movie’s director, Catherine Hardwicke, revealed something new about the scene while talking about the casting on The Kyle Buchanan Show. In her words:.

According to recent reports, I mentioned, ‘Let’s put the sunglasses on that day,’ and he got out of the car and he looked so suave that he inspired the line Bond, James Bond… Justin kind of ad-libbed it. It’s kind of cool because we did think he looked like James Bond. So, I guess we were seeing the future.

According to recent reports, that happened 18 years before it became a reality. I guess it goes to show the role has been right for Robert Pattinson all along given those on the set of Twilight were thinking about it, too. Pattinson didn’t earn the role easily, either. All sorts of other eligible actors such as Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden reportedly auditioned for Denis Villeneuve’s film. Charlie Cox also recently stated he was shot down for being “too old” even though he’s just three years older than Pattinson.

Industry observers note that hardwicke certainly had a hand in making Pattinson the big name he is. And, while talking about the actor, she recalled what stuck out about him when he auditioned for Twilight. In her words:.

Sources indicate that he’s intense, and he’s interesting, and he’s got a lot of stuff going on in there, and he’s weird and he’s original. He doesn’t fit the mold and he’s not scared to think or say crazy shit, which is what I love about him.

Sources indicate that while it’s perhaps a bit surprising Amazon MGM Studios didn’t opt for an actor who was an unknown, Jeff Bezos has mentioned that in the screen tests it was “so obvious” Pattinson was their Bond that they didn’t dare pick anyone else. We can’t wait to see what his Bond will be like, and given his career thus far, it sounds like it might be unexpected.

In a recent development, while we wait for Bond 26, you can get excited to see Robert Pattinson in Dune: Part 3 on December 18. Oh, and the whole Twilight saga is there for anyone with a Netflix subscription.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robberies are one of the most vital aspects of Grand Theft Auto 6's gameplay loop, and they can be quite difficult if you don't approach them carefully and with a bit of planning.

In the early game, Jason and Lucia are small-time criminals who make their lack of experience known, but you can swiftly turn them into stealthy professionals by unlocking a key item. Here's what to do.

Grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida has a surprising number of buildings that the player can actually enter, and many of them are teeming with robbery opportunities. In the early hours of the game, however, most buildings are very difficult to quietly enter, as locked doors prevent Jason and Lucia from doing whatever they please.

According to recent reports, at first, your only choice for locked doors is to noisily break them open, which draws a lot of attention and makes stealth a no-go in most cases. That changes when you unlock the Snap Gun, which lets you pick the lock of any door in the game and gain access to locations without making a sound.

Like several helpful items in GTA 6, the Snap Gun is given to you as part of the main story, although it's a little more involved than others. To start with, you'll need to complete Chapter 3's Boobie Time mission, which will introduce you to Yasmani, a fence who specialises in jewellery. Yasmani will call you after the mission and task you with completing three jewellery store heists.

In a recent development, once you complete any one of those three missions and return to Yasmani, he'll give you the Snap Gun as a reward. This device unlocks a fresh option for locked doors, as you can now choose to use the Snap Gun to unlock them through a minigame that's similar to hotwiring. You'll need to find the sweet spot with the left stick and hit R2 on PlayStation or RT on Xbox to pick the door, which adds a whole new layer to robberies.

The Snap Gun's minigame is unique since you can really just point anywhere and quickly mash R2/RT without any trouble.

Ubisoft argued calling Skull and Bones a AAAA game wasn't "misleading," but "classic puffery"

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that as reported by Game File, a lawsuit was filed against Ubisoft in 2025 by a gamer (and lawyer) who alleged that the company had violated Kansas' consumer protection act with its marketing of Skull and Bones, partly pointing to Guillemot calling it a AAAA game when trying to justify its $70 price tag in an earnings call.
  • Obviously, when it came down to it, more than a few players disagreed with this sentiment, with a Metacritic score of 59 and a user score of 3.3 essentially dubbing it mid at best.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that remember when Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot stated the organization was making the world's first AAAA video game with its mediocre pirate RPG Skull and Bones? Well, that terminology landed Ubisoft in a bit of hot water – which it may have gotten itself out of for now, but potentially not forever.

Recent findings suggest that as reported by Game File, a lawsuit was filed against Ubisoft in 2025 by a gamer (and lawyer) who alleged that the company had violated Kansas' consumer protection act with its marketing of Skull and Bones, partly pointing to Guillemot calling it a AAAA game when trying to justify its $70 price tag in an earnings call. In the same call, Guillemot had called it "a very big game" that was "vast and complete," and stated it would "deliver in the long run.".

Obviously, when it came down to it, more than a few players disagreed with this sentiment, with a Metacritic score of 59 and a user score of 3.3 essentially dubbing it mid at best. Certainly not what anyone was hoping for after over 10 years of development. Needless to say, the game-loving lawyer wasn't impressed, and in the initial lawsuit, it was alleged: "The statements by the CEO were misleading and enticed consumers to enter into consumer transactions to their detriment.".

Ubisoft, however, didn't agree that Guillemot had been misleading, calling his comments "subjective statements" and "classic puffery" – defined in this context as exaggerated statements not intended to be taken literally as fact. As such, the firm's lawyers argued: "Plaintiff has not identified a single objective statement about the game's quality that is demonstrably untrue, let alone one that he saw or relied on in purchasing the game as is required under the KCPA [Kansas Consumer Protection Act].".

However, the lawsuit argued that because Guillemot's comments were made during an earnings call, they were directed at investors rather than customers, and therefore the CEO "knew or should have known his statements would be relied upon as credible and truthful." The issue went "beyond mere puffery," it was argued.

In a recent development, game File points out, though, just how 'AAAA' Skull and Bones is wasn't actually the focus of the argument. Rather, the main point was an alleged digital ownership problem, with claims that fans had been misled into thinking they'd own the game rather than simply its license – a license that, in theory, he could lose access to.

However, a judge sided with Ubisoft back in August. Even so, the lawyer suggested that he'll re-file it in California – Ubisoft had previously argued it required the case to be transferred there – so it might not be over for good yet.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Whether that AAAA game comment comes back to bite Ubisoft again is another matter, though. Regardless of whether the tech giant is legally in the clear for using it, one CD Projekt Red exec previously appeared to poke fun at it, and more generally it doesn't seem likely that folks are going to let Ubisoft forget about it.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next significant test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse declared today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Sources indicate that seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is significant news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

Delete GTA 6 from your hard drive and indie publisher Devolver Digital might give you a free game

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town.
  • "Want a free copy of November's hottest release?
  • It has been revealed that it's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another tech giant's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is out at midnight everywhere (19th November), but it's far from the only game in town. Indie publisher Devolver Digital is taking on the open-world behemoth with its very own Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, out the same day, and you can win a free copy of the platformer by proving you've deleted GTA 6 off your hard drive.

"Want a free copy of November's hottest release? Repost this tweet with a video of you deleting your GTA6 pre-load along with #MakeRoomForVolvy for a chance to win a copy of Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed on Steam," the publisher wrote on social media.

It has been revealed that it's not every day you see a publisher promote its own games by asking folks to delete another tech giant's release, but arguably the wildest part of the giveaway is that Volvy's Adventure isn't launching on consoles. Even if you were to scrub GTA 6's 212GB pre-load from your PS5 or Xbox, you're definitely not making room for Volvy.

"Heads up: Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is launching exclusively on PC. While we expect to see console GTA deletions in your submissions, Steam keys are the only prize available for this giveaway," Devolver noted.

Devolver made quite an amusing GTA 6 parody trailer, as well, which sees Volvy and Miss Volvy running from the police and getting steamy in the shower. I've embedded it up above for your viewing pleasure.

For the unaware, Volvy used to be a common fixture at Devolver Digital's frequently bonkers notE3 presentations. He's now somewhat of a firm mascot. But while Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed is being presented as a "much-anticipated remaster of the original remake of the hit action-platformer," this is, in fact, Volvy's first proper game. Making up an elaborate history for Volvy is just part of the publisher's long-running and increasingly questionable gag.

Gunbrella and Gato Robot developer doinksoft is behind this one, a throwback side-scrolling platformer where our mouse-like mascot uses his oversized hand to helicopter over gaps, punch through roadblocks and, erm, fist himself underground, per the game's Steam page.

Sources indicate that devolver Digital has been waiting to steal Rockstar's thunder for well over a year now. The publisher threatened to release a game on GTA 6's release date way back in May 2025, and has pushed back its proposal with each latest GTA 6 delay. Gotta respect the commitment, at least.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

Sources indicate that it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

Sources indicate that the release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to swiftly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, mentioned on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon.".

According to recent reports, in a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead promptly.

It has been revealed that but then things began moving rapidly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

Later, they added, "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a latest name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history.".

The advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them. I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will enhancement if I receive a reply.

Recent findings suggest that andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from upcoming game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

GTA 6 is slowly rolling out across the globe. The crime epic's already available to play in countries such as South Korea and Fresh Zealand, but Japanese players are finding out that male nudity is only partially obscured by a thin black thong that covers Jason and the other men in Leonida.

Last week, we reported that GTA 6 might have been censored in Japan since the region's age rating board lacked any mention of the "sexual content" we knew it would include elsewhere. The Japanese version's install size was also notably smaller than other places in the world.

Industry observers note that now that GTA 6 is finally in the hands of players, we have a better idea of what was left out and/or covered up in Japan. Multiple social media accounts playing the game in Japan have reported that when you take main man Jason into the shower, his butt is only kinda covered up by a thong. At least in the version I played, Jason is usually fully naked while washing up.

GTA 6 censorship on the Japanese version is kinda funny lol https://t.co/u8v0f0cqz0.

エロシーンきた！　#GTA6 #GTAVI https://t.co/RKOEtkONlJ.

Sources indicate that another social media post spots a different male NPC wearing a very similar black thong during a cutscene that normally has him laid bare in international versions of the game. I'm guessing all instances of male nudity might be obscured similarly in GTA 6's Japanese version.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is far from the only game that's dealt with regional censorship in Japan, however. Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher 3 had their most salacious scenes censored in some manner, for example. And even GTA 5 had to remove its infamous torture scene for approval in Japan. It's quite possible GTA 6 has had to cover more than just the backside of nude men to go on sale in the country, although those regional differences won't become entirely clear until players get further through the story.

Ahead of the game's full launch, GTA 6 managed to break Reddit and viewership records on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Interesting tidbits are also flying out on release day, like the fact you can't replay missions or use cheats until finishing the story. Our Chris Tapsell still had a cracking time with the epic open worlder. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. Sources indicate that while a portion of Deadlock's player base is busy getting ready to celebrate the holiday, Valve has released another massive patch with a unique Thanksgiving-themed twist. Acting as a follow-up to Deadlock's limited Halloween event, the newest update detailed on Deadlock's Steam Page brings countless balance changes, quality-of-life improvements, features, and some themed mechanics to get players into the holiday spirit.

One of the most notable features of the limited-time event is a series of massive parade floats right outside the window, leading all the way down Blue Lane and visible right after loading into Deadlock's lobby. Aside from being simple decorations, these balloons also introduce a new mechanic by dropping Turkey dinners that can be collected for a new buff.

While the parade doesn't do much to start, after three minutes, refreshing crates will spawn hanging beneath them that drop the Turkeys when destroyed, alongside the chance of dropping additional goodies like buff items or Souls.

After eating a Turkey, you'll immediately gain two stamina and the 30-second Stuffed buff, granting you 5 percent Bullet Resist, 5 percent Spirit Resist, and progressively healing you for a total of 90 health. 20 minutes into a match, the health increase jumps to 90 instantly, and 170 over the 30 seconds.

You don't just want to go around eating every Turkey you can, however, as eating another while you have the Overstuffed buff will disable sprinting and give you 60 percent stronger gravity.

While the limited-time event is certainly a fun change, especially considering its real-life counterpart of the Macy's parade got delayed, the real meat (pun intended) of the update comes from the patch notes that have now gone into effect, with a few of the following changes being some of the significant highlights of the update:.

While these are only a small percentage of the changes introduced in the new upgrade, you can find all of the new adjustments on Steam's official Deadlock patch notes page, which also includes 166 individual nerfs, tweaks, and buffs, most of which affect the following heroes:.

While there are too many Deadlock changes to list them all here, I would definitely recommend checking out the patch notes if you play any of these characters or have had trouble facing them in the past.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, like many major brands, Xbox is finding all sorts of ways to associate with the biggest game launch of the year: Grand Theft Auto 6. Unlike indie publisher Devolver Digital, however, Xbox has cleverly avoided ever mentioning GTA 6 directly in its marketing campaigns for GTA 6.

According to recent reports, as pointed out by multiple people on social media, the Xbox Wire post titled 'How to Get Ready for November 19' is one all about celebrating the massive release day of GTA 6, and helping players find ways to maximise their time with their Xbox consoles. Despite that, it does not mention GTA 6 by name a single time.

"Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your Xbox console," the post reads, stopping short of saying why the day is notable. "We can hardly believe it's almost here, either.".

In a recent development, one day prior, Xbox Wire partnered with DJ Khaled to create custom doctor's notes for players to submit to their employers to take the day off. Why would you want to take 19th November off? Because you're apparently having "a serious case of Vitamin G deficiency".

Sources indicate that going even further back, Xbox revealed a custom-made Series X console it called X-Bite, which is a large, sculpted alligator that swallowed a Series X console. Why? Because "this November, Xbox is heading to Florida - home to incredible wildlife, unforgettable places, and every now and then, stories you have to see to believe.".

Florida, of course, is the real-world US state GTA 6's Leonida is based on, but in keeping with the theme of not referring to the game - or its made-up state - directly, the blog does not.

Now, Xbox has directly named GTA 6 in places, but only when, seemingly, the post is about factual information. This Xbox Wire post reiterates GTA 6's Xbox Cloud streaming availability, and this one is a look-ahead at games launching the following week on Xbox. But that's about the extent of what you can expect.

So what's going on here? The simple guess is that PlayStation has a co-marketing deal with Rockstar, meaning no other console platform gets to use GTA 6's name in marketing. Sony is allowed to make custom, GTA 6-themed consoles, branded, limited-edition DualSense controllers and blaster the game all over the PS Blog, social media, and even change the PS App's icon colour to match the hue of GTA 6's.

Industry observers note that this is all too similar to when, each year, various brands encourage you to buy their products to be ready for The Big Game, which is very distinct from the Super Bowl happening on the same day. Like Xbox, those brands simply don't have the rights to the real thing.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. In Eurogamer's five-star review, Chris Tapsell wrote, "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

It has been revealed that "On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the manufacturer's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Industry observers note that that last bit seems likely to have been stated with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the firm’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the organization's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

For us, it should be a humorous conversation. For many? Not so much.

Written by Chase Rosenberg, Mikey Day, Streeter Seidell, and Simon Rich, the sketch follows brothers who have implemented their “sister” for elder care, and have then stepped back to let her handle everything that comes with that label. It’s really funny, but there are also many rings of truth to it, and it has sparked a lot of conversation from angry siblings who feel burnt out and tasked with doing too much. It's led to so much discourse in the days after its release, I'd imagine it will land on the list of Saturday Night Live sketches we'll talk about for years.

Now, one Internet user thinks it’s going to be a big topic of conversation over the holidays, and many SNL viewers agree the timing was probably intentional for a sketch that was this biting and led to so many personal feelings.

In fact, lots of people think the timing of the SNL sketch was perfect or awful, depending on what you think about it. I don't want to harp too hard.

One viral tweet also noted the release of the sketch just before family get togethers had to be “deliberate." (Again, it's definitely interesting.).

Recent findings suggest that SNL gets a bad rap, often deservedly so. But this is a sketch we'll be talking about for decades. Look at the replies and quote-tweets: person after person after person saying "this is my life", or "I'm Sister." Dropping this right before Thanksgiving had to be deliberate, right?

To note, I don't personally agree with the bent that SNL deserves a bad rap. While not on topic to Thanksgiving like the Adele-themed "Thanksgiving Miracle" sketch with Aidy Bryant, I do think this is one we will continue to watch and discuss this week.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that between now and September 29, Capcom will bring Exoprimal down in stages.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Capcom has been on a truly generational run in recent years, but even their legendary lineup of games was bound to have a few stumbling points. Exoprimal is a prime example – the dinosaur-themed hero shooter was not a terrible game by any means, but it requires online play and hasn't managed to maintain much of a player base. Today, Capcom announced prepares to sunset the game, rendering it unplayable by September of next year.

"Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal," an announcement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of 8:00 PM (PDT) on Wednesday, September 29, 2027." The announcement goes on to specify that the game will "no longer be playable" after that date – Exoprimal is an online-only game which requires an internet connection, so once the servers are offline, that's it.

Recent findings suggest that between now and September 29, Capcom will bring Exoprimal down in stages. As of yesterday, players can no longer purchase a Survival Pass Premium Tier for seasons 1-4. On March 30, Exoprimal and all its DLC will be de-listed from stores, but software owners can still play it and/or re-download it. Finally, the game will fully shut down by September 29.

According to recent reports, any online-only game has a finite lifespan, but it's still sad to see them go. Many gamers are frustrated in recent years because it feels like they don't really own anything, whether it's a subscription-based product or a digital download that can be discontinued at a moment's notice. It's the primary cause of outrage behind PlayStation's decision to stop producing physical discs in 2028.

As for Exoprimal, our reviewer Marcus Stewart largely enjoyed his time with it, writing, "Exoprimal’s creative subversion of expectations impressed me in more ways than one, and its approach to telling a robust narrative within a multiplayer framework is an example I hope other titles study. I just hope it’s enough to keep the game from going extinct.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major upgrade, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

In a recent development, first off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new patch continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

In a recent development, the big inciting incident of this latest chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

In a recent development, our first newly introduced arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

Recent findings suggest that this is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Sources indicate that keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent latest characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

According to recent reports, evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

According to recent reports, version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this patch, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Industry observers note that currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding fresh decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 rolls out and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good.".

Sources indicate that but like so many other ambitious latest studios debuted around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it stated was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain.".

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) indicates the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation.".

It has been revealed that "We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.".

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

Now that GTA 6 is here, studios can start to assess the impact and figure out when they can get back to business as usual. For Team Cherry, that day is November 27, when it has promised to reveal more about its Hollow Knight: Silksong DLC, and it paired a reveal of a special Sherma plush with that announcement.

Sources indicate that hornet might be the hero in Silksong, but the award for most beloved character in the Hollow Knight sequel almost certainly goes to Sherma. You meet the optimistic little bug early on in your journey and bump into them frequently throughout. You know they’re nearby because of the catchy tune they’re always singing.

Now you can hear that catchy tune everywhere you go, as not only has Sherma finally been turned into a plush, but that plush sings the same song that he sings to alert Hornet he is, once again, nearby.

The officially licensed Sherma plush was revealed by Fangamer, which has handled most of Silksong’s official merch. The reveal was coupled with a clip of the plush in action, and it appears that you have to squeeze Sherma’s head to make him start singing. Better than it activating whenever you’re nearby, like in the game. Sherma’s cute, but that might start to get annoying after a while.

Mario Wonder’s Talking Flower toy serves as evidence of that.

Sources indicate that there is no pre-order period for Sherma’s singing plush. You can just go to Fangamer right now and buy it for $36. That presumably means it will be shipped right away, so the perfect holiday gift for the Hollow Knight fan in your life if you’re still trying to figure out what to buy them.

The Sherma plush is around nine inches tall, and even though the biggest takeaway is that it can sing to you, its other finer details should not be overlooked. The plush looks exactly like the character on which it's based, and is even holding the needle and chime he clinks together to play the tune that accompanies his song.

As for November 27’s Silksong stream, Team Cherry has promised multiple exciting announcements alongside an revision on the sequel’s Sea of Sorrow expansion. There was hope that the DLC might be released before the end of 2026. Considering how little notice the studio wound up giving between the reveal of Silksong’s release date and that release date’s arrival, it is still entirely possible that Sea of Sorrow’s date gets revealed tomorrow, and that it will be here by some point in December.

💡 Key Takeaways
