General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

How Nintendo Recovered After Stumbling In The Streetpass

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3080 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By the time Nintendo ceased production of the 3DS in September 2020, the company’s last dedicated line of exclusively handheld video game devices had completed one of gaming’s most incredible comebacks.
  • The move worked: In its first month at its new price, 3DS sales in America rose 260 percent.
  • One obvious problem with the launch was the games – or lack thereof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By the time Nintendo ceased production of the 3DS in September 2020, the company’s last dedicated line of exclusively handheld video game devices had completed one of gaming’s most incredible comebacks. But to come back, you must first fall, and fall the 3DS did soon after it first rolled out in February 2011: its first month-and-a-half sales numbers came in nearly 400,000 units short of Nintendo’s initial projections of 4 million units sold. Over the next three months, Nintendo sold just an additional 710,000 3DS units worldwide, with only 110,000 purchased in the United States. In response, Nintendo took drastic measures, slashing the 3DS price in America from $250 to $170 just a half-year after the handheld launched.

The move worked: In its first month at its new price, 3DS sales in America rose 260 percent. According to metrics released by Nintendo last year, the 3DS family of devices ended its run at a stunning 76 million units sold, still half of the original DS’s total but far more than other Nintendo platforms like the GameCube (21.7 million), Nintendo 64 (32.9 million), SNES (49.1 million), and even the original NES (61.9 million). The little system that couldn’t eventually proved it could.

One obvious problem with the launch was the games – or lack thereof. Included in the modest North American 3DS launch lineup were just three Nintendo first-party titles: Nintendogs + Cats, Pilotwings Resort, and Steel Diver. Though a Zelda remake, a new Mario platformer, and a new Mario Kart would arrive by year’s end, traditional system-selling franchises were initially nowhere to be found. By the time the bigger games arrived, Nintendo’s three first-party launch titles were placed in the dustbin of history, something Game Informer predicted in its review of Steel Diver, which labeled the game as “destined to become a strange and forgotten footnote in the publisher’s history.”.

Every first-party launch title communicates, both intentionally and unintentionally, something about the system upon which it’s launching and the company that created it. Last year, for instance, Mario Kart World evidenced that seamless open-world design and an interest in making buckets of money would remain hallmarks of Nintendo’s Switch 2 era. So, what can these three largely forgotten launch games tell us about the 3DS and Nintendo more broadly?

Recent findings suggest that initial hardware reviews of the 3DS contained two recurring thoughts: The glasses-free 3D effect was impressive when it worked – but it didn’t always work. Engadget’s review further hypothesized that “a lot of people are going to buy a 3DS and find they don’t really care for the 3D effect.” By the time Super Mario 3D Land released nine months after launch, Game Informer’s Bryan Vore was startled to find he was using the system’s primary feature at all, writing, “What surprises me most about 3D Land is how well the 3D effect is handled. I kept the 3D slider up most of the game”.

In a recent development, indeed, in Nintendo’s 2011 fiscal year report, president Satoru Iwata theorized that initial 3DS sales were underwhelming because the firm had not done a convincing enough job of explaining the system’s signature innovation to potential customers: “The value of 3D images without the need for special glasses is hard to be understood through the existing media. However, we have found that people cannot feel it just by trying out a device, rather, some might even misestimate it when experiencing the images in an improper fashion.” Just two and a half years after the system’s launch, Nintendo began selling a fully flattened version of the handheld, appropriately named the 2DS.

Part of the matter with the underwhelming launch was that the 3DS lineup lacked an obvious killer app: There was neither a clear game that made purchasing the handheld an easy decision, nor was there a game that immediately proved that the 3D effect was anything more than an optional gimmick. In fact, among the three first-party titles was a game that had been designed nearly to completion before the team even learned of the existence of the 3DS.

When Nintendo first began showing the original DS to journalists at E3 in 2004, included among upcoming releases, like Metroid Prime Hunters and WarioWare Touched!, was a humble submarine simulation tech demo. IGN’s hands-on preview called the sub demo “simple in concept, but surprisingly complex in its controls and gameplay,” noting that it was “one of those ‘fun, but not quite a full game’ games at Nintendo’s booth, so it’s hard to say if development teams will expand on Submarine’s design to make it a more complete package.” At first, the team that made the demo, comprising veterans from Star Fox and F-Zero, was also unsure if they would expand it into a full game, as many of its members began work on other projects like Wii Fit.

According to recent reports, much later, producer Tadashi Sugiyama stated in an Iwata Asks interview posted on Nintendo’s website that Nintendo of America asked the team to reconvene and release the submarine demo as downloadable software for the Nintendo DSi. But as the game – soon to be titled Steel Diver – expanded from just one mode (the side-scrolling submarine exploration and combat that would form the bulk of the game’s missions) to three modes (including Periscope Strike, a first-person torpedo shooter from the perspective of a periscope, and Steel Commander, a top-down strategy game partially inspired by the Japanese-exclusive 1990 Game Boy game Kaisen Game: Radar Mission), the Steel Diver team – now composed of both Nintendo designers and the 11 members of Giles Goddard’s company Vitei – decided to expand their demo into a full retail release. This initially led to an identity crisis for director Takaya Imamura, who revealed to Iwata that he briefly, “thought it would be fine to set the game in a flashy, glittery world like – and I’m not kidding – a submarine version of Mario Kart.” Sugiyama quickly shut that idea down, and the game proceeded with more traditional aquatic environments.

It has been revealed that highly invested in the project was the legendary Shigeru Miyamoto, who held a key piece of information from the team: Though Steel Diver was developed for the DS, he thought that it would make an even better showcase for the manufacturer’s yet-to-be-revealed 3DS. But it wasn’t until very late into the development process that the Steel Diver team even learned of the existence of the fresh console, a decision Miyamoto explained in Iwata Asks: “I knew the game was perfect for the Nintendo 3DS system, but I was afraid that if we switched from the Nintendo DS system to the Nintendo 3DS system in the middle of development, the contents wouldn’t be thoroughly fine-tuned. So after the Nintendo DS version was about done, I stated, ‘Let’s shift this over to the Nintendo 3DS system.’” According to Imamura, “[w]hen we heard that, we already had intends for debugging. Development was all but over.”.

Recent findings suggest that the process of adding an extra dimension to the game proved difficult at first, with Imamura telling Iwata, “We thought we could just switch it over and it would look stereoscopic, but when we did, we couldn’t see it. […] We were among the first to develop software for the Nintendo 3DS system, so a sufficient development kit didn’t exist at the time.” But then, “one day it suddenly started popping out,” Goddard noted in that same Iwata Asks article. And it came at just the right time, Goddard added: “It started looking 3D about the day before our presentation. If it hadn’t, the whole thing might have ended.” Ultimately, Imamura felt that the game had found its correct home on the 3DS, even if the process could have been improved: “I’m really glad we changed it over to the Nintendo 3DS system. But I think it would have turned out even better if Miyamoto-san had told us sooner that he wanted to make it for the Nintendo 3DS system [laughs]!”.

Recent findings suggest that when the Wii launched in 2006, it came bundled with a number of pre-installed “channels” – or what we would likely just call apps today. Among those was the Mii Channel, an avatar-maker co-directed by Animal Crossing and Splatoon creator Hisashi Nogami. In an Iwata Asks interview, Nogami remarked that something like the Miis was an idea Miyamoto “had wanted to realize for some time.” Nogami revealed that originally the “plan was to develop three games in which the same characters designed by the player would appear.” But as development on the Wii advanced, the concept had “broadened to encompass the entire Wii.” Miis were integral features of the Wii’s user-interface, appearing in a large number of games including, most importantly, the Wii’s landmark pack-in, Wii Sports, and becoming a defining aspect of Nintendo’s cultural identity. In a 2008 fiscal report Q&A, Iwata made clear just how seriously the organization viewed Miis as part of its brand, stating that, to “Nintendo, licensing Mii is identical to licensing Mario.” The Mii was now Nintendo, and it should be treated like its other icons.

Sources indicate that however, it was not immediately clear to the general public whether the Mii was tied specifically to the Wii – with which it shared all but one letter – or if it would become Nintendo’s default avatar-creation system for the next two decades-plus, as we now know it has. Having rolled out in 2004, the DS did not include native Mii creation software, but it showed the first small signs that the Mii would become a core part of the larger Nintendo ecosystem.

According to recent reports, first, the thrillingly titled DS exercise game Personal Trainer: Walking – released in 2008 in Japan and 2009 in America – tied players’ pedometer-tracked steps to Mii avatars, which could be imported over from the Wii’s Mii Channel. However, players who did not own a Wii could only choose Miis from a series of random presets; there was no way to create a custom Mii within the game itself. The first DS game to feature a full Mii creation suite was 2009’s Tomodachi Collection, a Japan-exclusive social simulation game that would receive a more widely released sequel on the 3DS in 2013/2014 (a third game will arrive later this year.) But only three other DS games featured Miis at all: Ide Yousuke’s Healthy Mahjong DSi, a Japan-exclusive downloadable mahjong game; Kuruma de DS, also exclusive to Japan, a GPS-connected title made in collaboration with Toyota and Honda that could only be used in select cars; and Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Echoes of Time, which could feature a Mii-emblazoned item only if the player was connected to someone playing on a Wii.

Sources indicate that it wasn’t until the 3DS that it became clear that Miis would truly migrate away from their home system. The 3DS was pre-installed with an avatar creation application called Mii Maker. One of the system’s novel features was “StreetPass,” a communication system that allowed players to exchange data with other nearby players. Its showcase app was StreetPass Mii Plaza, in which up to 10 Miis could congregate and compete in minigames. By the end of 2013, the 3DS even had its own version of Miiverse, the Mii-based social network that first appeared on the Wii U.

Recent findings suggest that the surest sign that Miis were here for good was Pilotwings Resort. The 3DS launch title was the third – and final, for now – entry in the Miyamoto-created Pilotwings franchise of flight-simulation games. Each of the previous games had also served as North American launch titles for their respective systems, with each game functioning as a technical showcase for its system’s upgraded graphical capabilities. 1991’s Pilotwings utilized the Super Nintendo’s Mode 7 graphics to deliver groundbreaking “3D” visuals, while 1996’s Pilotwings 64 gave players the chance to explore the Nintendo 64’s more authentically three-dimensional spaces. Pilotwings Resort continued this trend, affording early 3DS adopters a massive playground to experiment with the system’s stereoscopic 3D visuals.

The earlier Pilotwings were not full of classic Nintendo iconography, but Pilotwings Resort represented a major aesthetic break: Every character in the game was a Mii. This aligned the game more closely with a different recent – and more recognizable – Nintendo series: Wii Sports. The action of Pilotwings Resort even takes place on Wuhu Island, the fictional tropical location where 2007’s Wii Fit and 2009’s Wii Sports Resort were also set.

Sources indicate that the origins of the island, however, trace back even further. When Nintendo showcased the Wii to journalists in May 2006, Wii Sports contained an additional game that was cut from the final release: a flight simulator called Airplane, in which players soared above an unnamed island that bore a number of striking similarities to Wuhu. Interestingly, as detailed in a 2006 Eurogamer article, Nintendo reps were quick to downplay any connection between Wii Sports Airplane and the Pilotwings franchise, with Matthew Kumar writing, “It’s not a Pilotwings, they say, despite featuring a lovely, relaxing island which features small towns to buzz over, and tunnels to barnstorm. And, oh, you know, rings to fly through to get points.” Additionally, Kumar wrote, “It’s not entirely clear how this would fit into the Wii Sports range (or pack) or, despite what they say, if it is even intended to. But as a tech demo for that Pilotwings game they’re going to unveil at TGS or something, it’s brilliant and I’m gasping for more.” By the time Pilotwings Resort finally saw the light of day a half-decade later, the Wii Sports franchise – and its iconic Miis – had climbed so high up the hierarchy of Nintendo’s first-party franchises that IGN’s review of the game opened with, “Wii Sports Resort is back. Did you miss it?”.

Miis appeared throughout the 3DS’s lifetime. They served as player icons for games like Super Mario 3D Land and Kid Icarus: Uprising, even starring in their own idiosyncratic games like Tomodachi Life and Miitopia. Miis would also be baked into future systems like the Wii U, the Switch, and the Switch 2. But it was Pilotwings Resort – along with Mii Plaza – that showed Nintendo had bigger and more serious aspirations for the Mii outside of the Wii.

When the original Game Boy launched in 1989, arriving in tow was an accessory called the Game Link Cable. It allowed players to connect directly to other Game Boy systems, enabling competitive multiplayer sessions in early hits like Tetris. Seven years later, with the release of the first Pokémon games, the Game Link Cable found a newly introduced calling, allowing players to not just compete, but also to swap their pocket monsters with other players in their communities. In her book Super Nintendo: How One Japanese Tech giant Helped the World Have Fun, Keza MacDonald argues that this marked a turning point for Nintendo: “Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue’s emphasis on trading and sharing represented an inspired reinvention of the Game Boy Link Cable: Game Freak took a piece of technology that had been used exclusively for competition and made it about communication, as well.”.

Recent findings suggest that that design principle – that games were about sharing and communication, too – reached its apotheosis with the 3DS’s StreetPass feature, which allowed the system to actively and, more interestingly, passively communicate with other nearby 3DSs via locally established, internet-free connections, even when the console was set to sleep mode. At launch, StreetPass was most prominently featured in the preinstalled Mii StreetPass Plaza app, which included the game Find Mii, an RPG in which players’ parties were filled with Miis taken from other 3DSs they had passed by. As producer Kouichi Kawamoto told Kotaku’s Stephen Totilo, Find Mii emerged “from our drive to make players feel like they accomplish something by using StreetPass”. It was an idle game powered by physical activity. In doing so, StreetPass’s communication had taken the sharing principles of the Game Link Cable in an entirely novel direction.

Industry observers note that streetPass was also implemented into Nintendogs + Cats, the best-selling of the 3DS’s first-party launch titles. While Pokémon players of yore had to establish a physical connection to see other players’ collections, StreetPass enabled Nintendogs players to passively interact with other owners and their pets. You could take your 3DS on a walk to an actual dog park, for example, and if there were any other 3DS owners in range, you would head home with a series of journal entries featuring their Miis, their pets, any messages they’d sent, and perhaps even a gift. These Miis and their pets would also soon begin to populate the game in other ways: You might run into them on a walk or even compete against them in dog demonstrates. Nintendogs on DS featured a similar feature – Bark Mode – but it required more active participation from players; with StreetPass, community-building was now a low-effort exercise (often involving actual exercise).

In a recent development, streetPass was central to Nintendo’s conception of the 3DS. In an Iwata Asks article, the eponymous Iwata remarked that the concept of the 3DS was, “Carry Around, Affect Each Other and Something Fresh Every Day.” Nintendogs + Cats producer Hideki Konno further stated, “[W]hile it’s definitely okay to enjoy the game at home, I hope players will go out walking around with their Nintendo 3DS system as often as possible. There’s a lot for that purpose not just in Nintendogs + Cats, but built into the system itself”. StreetPass was exactly the kind of kooky invention upon which Nintendo made its name, and its legacy of encouraging players to explore the world lives on in mobile games like Pokémon Go.

The 3DS would soon find better games – and better sales – but its modest launch lineup contained plenty of insight. Steel Diver’s winding path towards release evidenced Nintendo’s unwavering commitment to its internal ideas – and its most legendary designer’s unconventional style of communication. Pilotwings Resort further established a core part of Nintendo’s brand identity, while Nintendogs + Cats showed that even the most straightforward of Nintendo sequels could still feature peculiar innovations. Stereoscopic 3D may not have been the future of gaming, but other elements of the 3DS have stayed with us forever.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs.
  • Sources indicate that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend.
  • These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

Sources indicate that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

In a recent development, cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their aims. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying newly introduced," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

According to recent reports, though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony intends to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

It has been revealed that disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, it has been a long old time since we've heard anything from Hideki Kamiya's YouTube channel. The legendary designer kept us fed with gossip, grievances, and game dev stories a couple of years back, but things have been quiet for almost a year now. Until this week, that is!

Yes, Kamiya has uploaded a newly introduced video, and it's just as packed with interesting tidbits as you would hope. One part that particularly caught our attention, however, was when the dev started talking about studios he'd love to collaborate with in the future, including a certain Substantial N.

"Maybe they hate me, but I love Nintendo," Kamiya jokes in his latest video (translated by Automaton), "so I think we may be able to do something together".

He doesn't go into any detail about what a Clovers X Nintendo collab might look like, but hey, there's nothing wrong with trying to manifest something by speaking it into existence.

Recent findings suggest that kamiya's collaboration bucket list doesn't end there, mind you. He goes on to say that he'd be game to work with Sony or Microsoft, Koei Tecmo on an Omega Force sequel, Square Enix on a King's Knight sequel, and Bandai Namco on a Tag Team Match: M.U.S.C.L.E. game. Dream significant, eh!

Recent findings suggest that perhaps most eye-catching, he also says that he'd like to team up with Konami on a Castlevania game: “We’ll definitely make Castlevania. If you let us work on it, we can make something truly insane, so just contact us and we’ll be at your service”. There's a bit of classic Kamiya definitive language going on there, so we wouldn't take that as an announcement just yet — especially while he still has Okami 2 in the pipeline.

They are some lofty goals, but we have to respect the ambition. Kamiya founded his newly introduced studio, Clovers, after leaving PlatinumGames back in 2023. He is currently working on the aforementioned Okami sequel with Capcom, where he will be back in the Director's seat.

What would your dream Kamiya X Nintendo collaboration be? Let us know in the comments.

"It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 releases on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining.
  • In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".
  • Recent findings suggest that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

Recent findings suggest that the animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a company that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

Recent findings suggest that the vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the tech giant and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

According to recent reports, "After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It notes a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.".

The obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent firm Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Industry observers note that echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's notable to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

"Rockstar has remarked it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace.
  • As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a fresh premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.
  • The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a fresh premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

It has been revealed that for most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis stated that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

In a recent development, unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just rolled out on consoles, the manufacturer may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the upcoming paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • It has been revealed that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

It has been revealed that "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Industry observers note that though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson said the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson noted, adding that websites may return in the future.

Recent findings suggest that "I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

"We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," noted Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a big shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore latest possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its big heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the upcoming Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.
  • The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons right now in the works, and a wealth of upcoming additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.
  • In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons right now in the works, and a wealth of upcoming additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

According to recent reports, the video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a fresh dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Recent findings suggest that perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#132155. I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1213 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1213 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed.
  • According to recent reports, A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite.
  • You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

According to recent reports, A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

Almost nothing here works, figuratively and literally. Within three minutes of the opening mission, before Madsen's undercover cop Tanner goes undercover, you're ordered to join some marked police cars to head for a bust – but because the rozzers' primary function is to give chase to you, later on, driving too close crosses their wires, provoking them into blue-on-blue ramming maneuvres. Later, in a motorbike sprint down an inexplicably exploding beach, cartel goons are positioned across the sand, presumably to take drama-enhancing pot shots. They're so slow, however, both to notice your presence and to physically raise their guns, that they're barely out of their idle animations by the time you whizz past. And your own guy isn't much better: an assassination mission, which ends with your target cornered from an elevated position, requires that you take a few steps backwards first, as Tanner can't drop his shootin' arms low enough to land a hit from the balcony he's on.

Industry observers note that unlike Vice City's Tommy Vercetti, he can at least swim, which by 2004 standards gives the seaside Miami and Nice maps a fair verisimilitude, particularly when a shot-up boat engine forces the abandoning of ship. No amount of product-of-its-time concessions, though, can account for how woodenly unpalatable the on-foot action is. Controls are stiff and shooting feels meaningless, with zero tangible sense of bullets being sent nor received; killing a man carries all the weight of just shouting at him to lie down, and if it weren't for sound effects and the dwindling health bar, I could park Tanner in front of a firing squad of identically-modelled thugs with almost zero impression that his lungs were filling with Uzi rounds.

In a recent development, driver, of course, began as a pure wheelman sim, later installments only letting you hoof it after someone at developers Reflections began smelling that Rockstar money. It was therefore always unlikely, even for the purported GTA killer, that this would achieve action-adventure sophistication in its bipedal bits. Even so, god, it's woeful. Stingy checkpointing also means that failure is often punished by having to replay those tedious, flavourless shootouts in full.

The driving is better, which is a bit like saying there's decent cheese in this cheese and smallpox toastie. It's reasonably slidey, when throwing the back end through a curving French alleyway, and in contrast to the gunplay, there is a somewhat realised tactility to ploughing around in two tonnes of rolling metal. It has problems of its own, mind. Cars feel okay when they're moving, but contact and crashes are leaden, sluggish, visually underwhelming occasions that I would call non-events, were they not so slow to recover from that a single nasty impact can scupper a timed mission. Granted, I quickly re-learned how vital it is to keep both eyes on the road, as other vehicles, pedestrians, lamposts, and other detritus tend to pop into existence some mere fifty feet in front of my speeding bumper.

The result, of both this graphical shortcoming and the overly punishing crashes, is a getaway car sim that too often encourages you to drive like cataract-ridden grandparent. Worse, whoever put Letty Ortiz in a lunchbox must have also been in charge of the engine noises, producing an array of miserable high-rev dins – especially for the motorbikes, which screech like amateurishly autotuned vacuum cleaners. There are also shades of that deranged cop AI in ordinary commuters, who I've repeatedly seen swerving and slaloming around empty lanes, seemingly for no reason beyond violent confusion.

Strangely enough, my 2026 return has largely dodged the game's infamous glitchiness, the worst instance of physics defiance being a garage door that appeared to lift Tanner into the air before propelling him, incorporeally, through the car shed's roof. I recall much worse, from the days when I'd have my dad rent it for me from Blockbuster. Mission-critical NPCs getting stuck on walls; flipped pursuit cars spinning endlessly; getting flung into space when walking on an overturned vehicle (a common occurrence, given the actual 'crawling out' animation sometimes failed to play, the game instead teleporting you onto the spring-loaded underside instead).

In a recent development, I've thus far escaped these, but as far as I know, they're still lurking dormant, and none of what I've witnessed with adult eyes has been funny or stupid enough to imbue Driv3r 3 The Third with a Wiseauean so-bad-it's-good quality. It's just bad. It was always bad. Why did I even entertain the possibility that it wasn't bad?

Reflections, to their credit, accepted their folly. Narratively unrelated sequel Driver: Parallel Lines tucked away a bin full of discarded copies, at least until Ubisoft bought up the series and patched it out, and for all the fantastical coma silliness of direct followup Driver: San Francisco, that was sensible enough to keep Tanner where he best belongs: hands on the wheel, foot on the gas, gun holstered. And was a far, far better game for it, too.

As 2011's San Francisco launch also remains the most recent Driver release, I regretfully can't end with the assurance that DrIIIver's legacy is a mere blip on a redeemed franchise. That stain stank, and did for ages, very possibly to the extent that GTA's one-time biggest rival never recovered.

Sources indicate that still, even if Reflections couldn't fully turn around their fortunes, the consistent improvement from this to Parallel Lines to San Francisco showed that they did learn something. Maybe so too did anyone else who went on to make an open-world action game. Which wouldn't be the worst outcome; after all, those who do not learn from gnarled, stinking wrecks like this are doomed to repeat them.

In a shocking move – unless you know your Tolkien, that is – Sauron surrendered at the feet of Pharazon and Numenor's forces. With The Dark Lord seemingly in their captivity, it puts an intriguing twist on future seasons – and the potential desire to harbor an enemy within their gates.

Sources indicate that that is something the showrunners have already considered. Speaking to TV Insider, McKay remarked, "Maybe we start the next season with that exact question. 'What the hell are we supposed to do with him?' How do you actually handle a demigod who has surrendered to you? I think that’s a question worthy of exploration.".

Industry observers note that mcKay added, "Certainly there’s a precedent that if he shows humility, it can potentially give him control of an unwilling adversary. Maybe he’s learning from that precedent in this instance.".

Recent findings suggest that on another pressing question – why didn't they kill Sauron? – Payne pointed to the season 2 prologue, starring Jack Lowden as an earlier incarnation of the Dark Lord, as to why that would have been a foolish notion.

Industry observers note that "That’s the true thing about Maiar. We’ve shown in our show that the orcs tried that, and he came back as a black goo monster and ultimately re-instantiated," Payne explained.

Fear not, we're definitely getting answers to what Sauron will be up to in Numenor. Amazon officially greenlit The Rings of Power season 4 earlier this week, with filming set to begin next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other big-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

Sources indicate that that's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were newly introduced releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a substantial slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

According to recent reports, in Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything newly introduced, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Landon Tresp told the BBC that he and the anonymous girl "kind of just clicked" when they started chatting online while playing Among Us.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 17-year-old girl who had been missing for more than a year was rescued and returned home by the FBI after a friend she made while playing Among Us, and his mother, were able to track down her location and pass it along to law enforcement.

Landon Tresp told the BBC that he and the anonymous girl "kind of just clicked" when they started chatting online while playing Among Us. She eventually told Tresp she was a runaway who'd been held against her will for more than a year. After learning more, Tresp, 16, told his mother, Khristina, about the exchange; she was initially suspicious, but after speaking with the girl directly on Discord and reading reports of her disappearance, she took action, asking for a piece of mail or document with a full name on it, which the girl provided.

With that, Khristina began digging into tax and property records to find relevant addresses, which she then used to find photos on real estate sites. She showed the photos to the missing girl on Discord, who picked out the one where she was being held; with that information in hand, Khristina contacted the girl's mother on social media and spoke to her briefly on the telephone, and also received a call from the FBI asking if she could confirm that the girl was still alive.

"I mentioned: 'I have; I video chatted with her, I've seen her'," Khristina told the BBC. "And she goes 'Oh my God, I cannot believe any of this'.".

It has been revealed that the kidnapped girl contacted Khristina the following morning, after her alleged captor, 39-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel, had left the house. In a conversation monitored by the FBI, she stated she'd met Harmel on social media, where he'd pretended to be disabled and offered to pay her to help him get from Utah to Oregon. When he picked her up, however, he threw her phone into a river, then drove her to Oregon.

Recent findings suggest that the girl told Khristina that she was kept in his basement and forced to sleep against the wall in his bed, while he kept a knife under his pillow to prevent escape. He gave her a mobile phone that wasn't able to make calls but could connect to wifi, which is how she was able to play online and eventually reach out for help.

According to recent reports, while Harmel was out, law enforcement began monitoring his street and house; when the moment came, police had Khristina tell the victim that it was time to make her escape. She was able to leave the house safely and into the custody of state troopers, while Harmel was subsequently arrested and charged with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

A social media post by the Salt Lake City FBI confirmed the outcome, although the crucial role played by Landon and Khristina Tresp was omitted: It states only that "the FBI and the Rich County Sheriff’s Office have been actively investigating this case for more than a year and pursuing every lead received from across the US and in other countries.".

Sources indicate that A separate Department of Justice press release, however, acknowledges that "on Nov. 1, the FBI received a tip about the possible location of the minor victim and that the victim met Harmel on a social media application in May 2025.".

In a recent development, khristina and Landon have remained in daily contact with the girl they helped rescue, and they're trying to arrange an in-person meetup as well. "Sometimes we just sit on video chat, just so she knows she has someone that cares," Khristina said. "She was on video last night when I cooked dinner …it's nice to know that when she has a bad day or a bad moment, she can call me right away or call Landon right away. She's doing great for what she's gone through.".

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1339 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nintendolife ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Feature: 8 Ways To Make Zelda: Ocarina Of Time More Difficult

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1339 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While it's less likely for players enjoying Ocarina of Time for the first time, veterans may well find the game a bit easy.
  • In a recent development, more than just knowing the geography and where to find key items, certain enemies feel less threatening in the remake.
  • It's a welcome change in most cases (those green things, in particular, were a damn nuisance), but if this isn't your first rodeo — and with no Master Quest to turn to (yet) — you may be looking for ways to spice things up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While it's less likely for players enjoying Ocarina of Time for the first time, veterans may well find the game a bit easy.

In a recent development, more than just knowing the geography and where to find key items, certain enemies feel less threatening in the remake. Tektites, Peahats, those spinny green things outside the Spirit Temple - many enemies aren't the obstacles they once were, meaning the adventure goes down smoother than ever.

It's a welcome change in most cases (those green things, in particular, were a damn nuisance), but if this isn't your first rodeo — and with no Master Quest to turn to (yet) — you may be looking for ways to spice things up.

So, today we'll take you through a handful of methods to up the difficulty and make your quest to save Hyrule a little less forgiving.

First up, it's an oldie but a goodie: the classic don't-level-up mode.

In a recent development, akin to an SL1 (Soul Level 1) run in Dark Souls and its ilk, this is a simple restriction where you just don't collect any Heart Containers. You'll need to get through the game with just the three hearts you start with, hence the name.

Industry observers note that having so little life obviously means you need to up your combat game, with stronger enemies able to take you out in a single hit. Shield work, dodging, and spot-on timing are requirements, and you'll need to stock up on potions if you're heading into Death Mountain crater without the right tunic. Business Scrub seeds are also useful if you're mid-dungeon and could do with a refill.

It's definitely worth tracking down all the bottles and stocking up on fairies for a three-heart run - that is unless you're adding more self-imposed restrictions to make things tougher still.

While the Gold Skulltulas themselves don't bestow any goodies, the rewards collected from the cursed home in Kakariko Village are useful - particularly the Adult's and Giant's Wallets.

Recent findings suggest that not having those means you'll be strapped for cash at certain points, unable to purchase useful equipment. The Child's Wallet only holds 200 rupees, so seeing that the Great Fairies in the remake now charge for their services, you'll miss out on a couple of handy buffs. That's right, no Nayru's Love for you.

Everything you need to finish the game is obtainable by other means, but this just makes it more challenging. Which is why you're here, right?

In a recent development, alternatively, you can avoid the Great Fairies altogether. Well, all except one.

Throughout Hyrule, these large women offer buffs and spells, but only one of them is necessary to progress through the game. You'll save yourself some cash by avoiding them, although losing the magic and health upgrades will sting. A great way to test your mettle, though.

It has been revealed that this is a fairly minor tweak that won't impact difficulty much for veteran Heroes of Time, but not being able to see your status at a glance does change things. (In fact, as reminded by Citrus_Architect in the comments, it also turns off your reticule for some added aiming challenge.).

According to recent reports, more than difficulty, though, heading to the settings and enabling 'Master' mode turns off not just the UI, but also Navi's pop-up dialogue boxes. This means you won't have her commentary to help you, or tell you, for example, that the water falling from the sky is rain.

A swordless Ocarina run does what it claims on the tin: Can you beat the game without using a sword?

Some purists go further and use glitches and bugs to avoid even collecting or touching any sort of blade — which makes things particularly challenging once you open the Door of Time — but just not using a sword (or a 'knife', cheaters) sounds tricky enough.

According to recent reports, using bottles to deflect lightning balls is a neat trick carried over from the original, and with sword alternatives including sticks, hammers, and bombs, it's possible to get much further than you think. The original presented difficulties, especially with bosses (hi, Bongo Bongo), but it wasn't technically possible to finish the final fight without a blow from The Blade of Evil's Bane.

Sources indicate that so what about the remake? Well, star0chris went for it recently in the video above (spoilers, obviously). Let's just say it's a faithful remake.

According to recent reports, another addition to the remake is microphone support for Ocarina input. This lets you hum tunes if you prefer, but selecting 'Instruments' means the mic will listen for...well, you'll never guess.

In one way, not having to memorise the button combos for the songs might be easier. And if you already play an instrument and know the notes, this is going to be a neat novelty more than a challenge.

According to recent reports, the real challenge comes when if you don't know how to play the ocarina/guitar/keyboard/oboe and have to learn to get through the game. You probably don't need 10,000 hours to bosh out eight notes, but it'll still take dedication. And no cheating with Hori's electronic ocarina.

If you're wondering which instruments work, Parker Deal on YouTube exhaustively tested over 50 musical instruments in the video above so you don't have to.

In the original, not pressing 'Z' at all means that you can't recentre the camera behind Link, so if you're looking to replicate this particular self-imposed challenge mode in the remake, consider not touching the right stick as well.

The main problem, though, is losing the ability to lock onto enemies, so crowd control becomes more difficult, and Keese can go from irksome to deadly when you can't easily track the bat's position.

Gyro aiming is a massive help in the newer version, but nuking that and camera control is possibly a bit much. Not being able to lock on to targets should prove challenging enough unless nothing but Nightmare! mode will do.

Finally, the connoisseur's choice. Is there any other tool the discerning 64-bit gamer would use to save Hyrule?

According to recent reports, using the Nintendo Switch Online N64 controller does present some input challenges, however. It enforces a swordless run because the Joy-Con's 'Y' isn't mapped to the N64 pad and it isn't right now possible to remap buttons on this particular controller.

'X' also has no counterpart, although you can switch 'X' and 'B' via the in-game menus, so you can jump. Beyond that, the right stick camera controls map to the 'C' buttons, 'A' rolls and dashes as you'd expect, the D-pad works exactly as it does on a Pro Controller, and the tiny additional 'ZR' button on top becomes your item button. Without your sword, expect to be pressing that a lot.

And no 'X' or 'Y' for your ocarina notes? No problem! Remember you can hum the tunes and the console will register them (most of the time).

Honestly, along with the Master Quest, I've got my fingers crossed that Nintendo patches in proper N64 controller support. It works perfectly with Star Fox, Switch 2's other 64-bit remake, and they patched support into Super Mario 3D All-Stars.

Until then, this feels like No Sword+ mode.

Sources indicate that and finally, if you're a total masochist, you could try all of the above: using the N64 pad with Master mode UI, no hearts, no Gold Skulltulas, no Great Fairies, no Z-targeting, and only using real instruments to play the ocarina. The odds are against you and the situation's grim.

So, there's a selection of ways to make Ocarina a bit more challenging, at least until the rumoured Master Quest arrives to shake things up.

Of course, the sky's the limit when it comes to self-imposed restrictions. Some further suggestions:.

Let us know which of these 'modes' tickles your fancy — and if you've tried any of them out — in the poll and comments below.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shortly it debuted back in 2009, Ryan Murphy's campy musical comedy Glee became a sensation.
  • Monteith's death broke the heart of fans and his coworkers alike, with the cast swiftly putting together a tribute episode in the midst of their grief.
  • My response to the Glee curse, as it’s always been, is we are human.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shortly it debuted back in 2009, Ryan Murphy's campy musical comedy Glee became a sensation. The series (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) broke barriers in regards to LGBTQ+ representation, and also featured plenty of memorable musical numbers. The show has also been associated with a number of tragedies, with three main cast members having died, starting with Cory Monteith's death back in 2013. There's been chatter online about the "Glee curse" and now Tina actress Jenna Ushkowitz has issued a heartfelt response about that discourse.

Monteith's death broke the heart of fans and his coworkers alike, with the cast swiftly putting together a tribute episode in the midst of their grief. Since then there's been more tragedies with this talented ensemble, such as Naya Rivera's death in 2020. While appearing on the podcast We Need To Talk with Paul C. Brunson, Ushkowitz shared her emotional reaction to folks insensitively talking about the Glee curse.

My response to the Glee curse, as it’s always been, is we are human. And to hear that people see this as a collective curse that’s like, ‘Who’s next?’ is so unkind. And it highlights the way in which we are able to just sit behind our computers and type off whatever we think we’re feeling in that moment without really connecting to what’s behind it and who’s on the other side.

Talk about honesty. While folks online might be talking about the show's curse with levity, the experience of those who actually worked on Glee is another one entirely. Real people died, not characters, which has been a source for quite a bit of pain by the rest of the cast. Those feelings remain to this day, case in point being Harry Shum Jr. honoring Naya Rivera this season on Dancing with the Stars.

In addition to the death of Rivera and Monteith, Puck actor Mark Salling committed suicide back in 2018 before going to prison for possession of child sexual abuse imagery. What's more, an entire docuseries called The Price of Glee was released in 2023 examining the "curse." In the same podcast, Jenna Ushkowitz spoke more about the pain and grief that the cast has dealt with, offering:.

We lost friends. People grieve those people. This is not something that’s, like, ‘Who’s next? This is a game.’ It’s not.

Industry observers note that the internet can be a cruel place, and the discourse about the Glee curse has clearly been painful for the cast. The tragic loss of their coworkers is hard enough, but the light-hearted chatter about these deaths has clearly created more pain for the members of the William McKinley High School Glee Club. Hopefully Ushkowitz's comments will circulate online, and help to quiet that type of talk.

According to recent reports, glee is streaming in its entirety over on Hulu, while fans patiently wait for news about Ryan Murphy's potential reboot. Our thoughts continue to be with the cast as they process their grief.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

It has been revealed that the game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The latest season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

Industry observers note that the even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The newly introduced season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Recent findings suggest that blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In a recent development, in case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next major enhancement, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive organization’s debut on Valve’s platform.

Industry observers note that the main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as Latest Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

Sources indicate that the release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two newly introduced arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

According to recent reports, the first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver major Physical burst damage.

It has been revealed that the higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this revision is the upcoming Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

In a recent development, when an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

It has been revealed that the Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a latest Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Closing statements in Rockstar and IWGB's employment tribunal case - revolving around the GTA 6 developer's alleged 'union busting' and the firing of 34 employees - have now been read, bringing the hearing to an end. There's currently no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

It has been revealed that the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

People Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as promptly as I possibly can.".

Industry observers note that however, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they remarked. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the new depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

It has been revealed that yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

Additionally, Rockstar employees are at the moment voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

It's called Silk and Silver (read my impressions), is all about merchant republics, and shipped alongside a beefy free enhancement to the base game which - while largely focused on overhauling economics - also has some funny patch notes and features worth being aware of.

According to recent reports, the main features of the free 'Florin' enhancement are outlined by Paradox in the video above, and unless you're really into the nitty gritty details of realm and wealth management, there's one bit of it which stands out. The option to play as a landless adventurer has finally made its way into the base game, as Paradox promised earlier this year.

This means you can kick off a playthrough as a lowborn leader of a travelling band or a wandering noble with claims on realms ruled by others. Originally locked behind the Roads to Power DLC, the option to start off this way or end up living if you end up deposed from your throne of choice is a great addition to the story arc of any CK3 run. No longer are you glued to the throne from day one to the day you quit for good - power's a privilege which can be earned and revoked depending on what you get up to. Though, it's worth noting that only three ways of operating as a landless adventurer are being made free to access with this revision. You can be an aimless wanderers, sword-toting mercenaries, or scholars. If you want your band to earn their living as explorers, free booters, or legitimists, you'll still need Roads to Power.

As for the rest of the free additions, community manager Jacob Blakey summed them up thusly:.
